", tostring(err))
	writeProgress("error", 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
end
__INDEX_GEN____INDEX_MAX_SCRIPTS____INDEX_MAX_SOURCE____INDEX_MAX_TOTAL__-- Real MCP UI inspection: what the player can actually see right now, as instance paths the other
-- tools can act on. A screenshot shows pixels; this returns the path you can click, read or write.

local __uiTracked = {
	ScreenGui = true, SurfaceGui = true, BillboardGui = true,
	Frame = true, ScrollingFrame = true, CanvasGroup = true,
	TextLabel = true, TextButton = true, TextBox = true,
	ImageLabel = true, ImageButton = true, ViewportFrame = true, VideoFrame = true,
}
local __uiInteractive = { TextButton = true, ImageButton = true, TextBox = true }
local __uiTextual = { TextLabel = true, TextButton = true, TextBox = true }
local __uiImage = { ImageLabel = true, ImageButton = true }

-- Visible means every GuiObject ancestor is visible too, up to the LayerCollector, which must be
-- enabled. A single hidden parent hides the whole subtree, so checking the leaf alone lies.
local function uiVisibleChain(inst)
	local current = inst
	while current do
		local okIsGui, isGui = pcall(function()
			return current:IsA("GuiObject")
		end)
		if not (okIsGui and isGui) then
			break
		end
		local okVis, visible = pcall(function()
			return current.Visible
		end)
		if okVis and visible == false then
			return false
		end
		current = current.Parent
	end
	-- current is now the LayerCollector (ScreenGui/SurfaceGui/BillboardGui) or nil.
	if current then
		local okEnabled, enabled = pcall(function()
			return current.Enabled
		end)
		if okEnabled and enabled == false then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

local function uiPreview(inst, className, previewLen)
	local text
	if __uiTextual[className] then
		local ok, value = pcall(function()
			return inst.Text
		end)
		if ok and value then text = tostring(value) end
	elseif __uiImage[className] then
		local ok, value = pcall(function()
			return inst.Image
		end)
		if ok and value and value ~= "" then text = "img=" .. tostring(value) end
	end
	if not text or text == "" then return nil end
	text = text:gsub("[\r\n\t]+", " ")
	if #text > previewLen then text = text:sub(1, previewLen) .. "\u{2026}" end
	return text
end

local function dumpVisibleUi(p)
	local maxItems = math.clamp(tonumber(p.maxItems) or 150, 1, 1000)
	local previewLen = math.clamp(tonumber(p.previewLen) or 80, 8, 400)
	local includeOffscreen = p.includeOffscreen == true
	local interactiveOnly = p.interactiveOnly == true

	local viewport
	local okCam, camera = pcall(function()
		return workspace.CurrentCamera
	end)
	if okCam and camera then
		local okVp, size = pcall(function()
			return camera.ViewportSize
		end)
		if okVp then viewport = size end
	end

	-- Three roots: the player's own GUI, the executor's hidden container, and CoreGui. gethui is
	-- where other executors park their UI, so it is the one that finds what a plain walk misses.
	local roots = {}
	local okPg, playerGui = pcall(function()
		return game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer.PlayerGui
	end)
	if okPg and playerGui then roots[#roots + 1] = { name = "PlayerGui", inst = playerGui } end
	if typeof(gethui) == "function" then
		local okHui, hui = pcall(gethui)
		if okHui and hui then roots[#roots + 1] = { name = "gethui", inst = hui } end
	end
	local okCore, coreGui = pcall(function()
		return game:GetService("CoreGui")
	end)
	if okCore and coreGui then roots[#roots + 1] = { name = "CoreGui", inst = coreGui } end

	local results, total, scanned = {}, 0, 0
	for _, root in ipairs(roots) do
		local okKids, kids = pcall(function()
			return root.inst:GetDescendants()
		end)
		if okKids and typeof(kids) == "table" then
			for _, inst in ipairs(kids) do
				scanned = scanned + 1
				-- A UI-heavy place has thousands of descendants; yield so the frame does not hitch.
				if scanned % 1500 == 0 then task.wait() end

				local className = inst.ClassName
				if __uiTracked[className] and not (interactiveOnly and not __uiInteractive[className]) then
					local okGui, isGuiObject = pcall(function()
						return inst:IsA("GuiObject")
					end)
					local keep = true
					local position, size

					if okGui and isGuiObject then
						local okSize, absSize = pcall(function()
							return inst.AbsoluteSize
						end)
						local okPos, absPos = pcall(function()
							return inst.AbsolutePosition
						end)
						if not (okSize and okPos) then
							keep = false
						else
							size, position = absSize, absPos
							-- Zero-area elements are laid out but invisible to the user.
							if absSize.X <= 0 or absSize.Y <= 0 then keep = false end
							if keep and not includeOffscreen and viewport then
								if
									absPos.X + absSize.X < 0
									or absPos.Y + absSize.Y < 0
									or absPos.X > viewport.X
									or absPos.Y > viewport.Y
								then
									keep = false
								end
							end
						end
						if keep and not uiVisibleChain(inst) then keep = false end
					else
						-- A LayerCollector has no geometry; keep it only if it is enabled.
						local okEnabled, enabled = pcall(function()
							return inst.Enabled
						end)
						if okEnabled and enabled == false then keep = false end
					end

					if keep then
						total = total + 1
						if #results < maxItems then
							local entry = {
								ClassName = className,
								Path = inst:GetFullName(),
								Root = root.name,
								Interactive = __uiInteractive[className] == true,
							}
							if position then
								entry.Position = { x = position.X, y = position.Y }
							end
							if size then
								entry.Size = { x = size.X, y = size.Y }
							end
							entry.Text = uiPreview(inst, className, previewLen)
							results[#results + 1] = entry
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end

	return {
		ok = true,
		viewport = viewport and { x = viewport.X, y = viewport.Y } or nil,
		count = total,
		returned = #results,
		limited = total > #results,
		elements = results,
	}
end
local __JOB = "__JOB_ID__"
local __genv = getgenv()
__genv.__mcp_jobs = __genv.__mcp_jobs or {}
local __slot = { cancelled = false, status = "running" }
__genv.__mcp_jobs[__JOB] = __slot
local __t0 = os.clock()
local __out = {}
local __progress = nil
local __rp, __rw = print, warn
local function __join(...)
	local n = select("#", ...)
	local parts = table.create(n)
	for i = 1, n do parts[i] = tostring((select(i, ...))) end
	return table.concat(parts, "\t")
end
local function __elapsed() return math.floor((os.clock() - __t0) * 1000) end
-- Bounded so a job that prints in a loop cannot grow the file without limit. The oldest lines go,
-- because the newest are the ones that say what it is doing now.
local function __push(line)
	__out[#__out + 1] = line
	if #__out > 400 then table.remove(__out, 1) end
end
local function print(...) __push(__join(...)) pcall(__rp, ...) end
local function warn(...) __push("[warn] " .. __join(...)) pcall(__rw, ...) end
local function __write(status, result, err)
	local payload = {
		jobId = __JOB,
		status = status,
		elapsedMs = __elapsed(),
		progress = __progress,
		output = table.concat(__out, "\n"),
		result = result,
		error = err,
	}
	local ok, text = pcall(encode, payload)
	if not ok then
		text = '{"jobId":"' .. __JOB .. '","status":"error","error":"failed to encode job state"}'
	end
	pcall(writefile, "mcp/jobs/" .. __JOB .. ".json", text)
end

␀#Í@␀␀␀—␀␀␀␀␀␀¿¿¿␀-- Real MCP closure spy: hook a live function and record what it is called with. Remote-spy answers
-- "what went to the server"; this answers "what was this local function handed", which is how you
-- read a client-side validator, a damage calculator or an anti-cheat check.

local __spyRegistry = getgenv()
__spyRegistry.__real_spies = __spyRegistry.__real_spies or {}
local __spies = __spyRegistry.__real_spies

-- Hooking one of these deadlocks us: the log builder itself calls tostring, so a hooked tostring
-- re-enters the hook forever and the whole client wedges. Keyed by function identity, not by name,
-- so `local p = print` is caught too.
local function spyHotBlocklist()
	local blocked = {
		[print] = "print",
		[warn] = "warn",
		[error] = "error",
		[pcall] = "pcall",
		[xpcall] = "xpcall",
		[select] = "select",
		[tostring] = "tostring",
		[tonumber] = "tonumber",
		[type] = "type",
		[typeof] = "typeof",
		[rawget] = "rawget",
		[rawset] = "rawset",
		[require] = "require",
		[table.insert] = "table.insert",
		[table.concat] = "table.concat",
		[task.wait] = "task.wait",
		[task.spawn] = "task.spawn",
		[task.defer] = "task.defer",
	}
	return blocked
end

local function spyPreview(value, maxLen)
	local ok, text = pcall(tostring, value)
	if not ok then return "<unreadable>" end
	if #text > maxLen then text = text:sub(1, maxLen) .. "\u{2026}" end
	return text
end

local function spyStart(p)
	if typeof(hookfunction) ~= "function" or typeof(newcclosure) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "hookfunction/newcclosure are not available in this executor" }
	end
	local source = p.getter
	if type(source) ~= "string" or source == "" then
		return { ok = false, error = "getter must be a Luau expression that resolves to a function" }
	end

	local chunk, compileErr = loadstring("return " .. source, "real-spy-getter")
	if not chunk then
		return { ok = false, error = "getter did not compile: " .. tostring(compileErr) }
	end
	local okRun, target = pcall(chunk)
	if not okRun then
		return { ok = false, error = "getter errored: " .. tostring(target) }
	end
	if type(target) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "getter resolved to " .. typeof(target) .. ", not a function" }
	end

	local blocked = spyHotBlocklist()
	if blocked[target] then
		return {
			ok = false,
			error = "refusing to hook the hot global '" .. blocked[target] .. "': the log builder calls it, so hooking it deadlocks the client",
		}
	end

	-- The pointer text doubles as a stable identity, so re-hooking the same function is a no-op.
	local spyId = tostring(target):gsub("function: ", "")
	if __spies[spyId] then
		return { ok = true, spyId = spyId, status = "already-hooked", calls = __spies[spyId].calls }
	end

	local maxLog = math.clamp(tonumber(p.maxLog) or 50, 1, 200)
	local argPreview = math.clamp(tonumber(p.argPreview) or 120, 16, 500)
	-- The hooked function itself is kept, not just the original it returned: restorefunction takes the
	-- TARGET as its first argument, so without this there is nothing to hand it and stop cannot undo
	-- anything.
	local spy = { calls = 0, log = {}, maxLog = maxLog, hooked = true, label = p.label, target = target }

	spy.original = hookfunction(
		target,
		newcclosure(function(...)
			spy.calls = spy.calls + 1
			-- checkcaller keeps our own calls out of the log and stops the hook re-entering itself.
			if not checkcaller() then
				local count = select("#", ...)
				local args = table.create(count)
				for i = 1, count do
					args[i] = spyPreview((select(i, ...)), argPreview)
				end
				local where
				local okInfo, src = pcall(debug.info, 2, "s")
				local okLine, line = pcall(debug.info, 2, "l")
				if okInfo then where = tostring(src) .. ":" .. tostring(okLine and line or "?") end
				-- Keep the LAST maxLog calls, not the first: the interesting call is usually the
				-- one you just triggered, and a first-N buffer fills up and then ignores it.
				if #spy.log >= spy.maxLog then table.remove(spy.log, 1) end
				table.insert(spy.log, { n = spy.calls, at = os.clock(), from = where, args = args })
			end
			return spy.original(...)
		end)
	)

	__spies[spyId] = spy
	return { ok = true, spyId = spyId, status = "hooked", label = p.label }
end

local function spyStop(p)
	local spy = __spies[p.spyId]
	if not spy then return { ok = false, error = "no spy with id " .. tostring(p.spyId) } end
	if typeof(restorefunction) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "this client has no restorefunction, so the hook cannot be removed" }
	end
	-- restorefunction(target, original): the first argument is the function that was hooked. Passing
	-- the returned original instead - which is what this used to do - restores nothing and reports no
	-- error, so the hook stayed live while the registry entry was deleted, leaving it unreachable.
	local ok, err = pcall(restorefunction, spy.target, spy.original)
	if not ok then
		return {
			ok = false,
			spyId = p.spyId,
			error = "could not unhook: " .. tostring(err) .. ". The spy is left registered so it can be stopped again.",
		}
	end
	-- Verify rather than assume. isfunctionhooked answers directly, and a stop that silently did
	-- nothing is exactly the failure this whole change is about.
	local stillHooked = nil
	if typeof(isfunctionhooked) == "function" then
		local okH, h = pcall(isfunctionhooked, spy.target)
		stillHooked = okH and h or nil
	end
	if stillHooked == true then
		return {
			ok = false,
			spyId = p.spyId,
			error = "restorefunction ran but the function still reports as hooked. Leaving the spy registered.",
		}
	end
	spy.hooked = false
	__spies[p.spyId] = nil
	return { ok = true, spyId = p.spyId, status = "stopped", calls = spy.calls, verified = stillHooked == false }
end

local function spyList()
	local out = {}
	for spyId, spy in pairs(__spies) do
		out[#out + 1] = { spyId = spyId, label = spy.label, calls = spy.calls, logged = #spy.log, hooked = spy.hooked }
	end
	return { ok = true, count = #out, spies = out }
end

local function spyLogs(p)
	local spy = __spies[p.spyId]
	if not spy then return { ok = false, error = "no spy with id " .. tostring(p.spyId) } end
	local limit = math.clamp(tonumber(p.limit) or 25, 1, 200)
	local out = {}
	-- Newest first: the call the caller just provoked is the one they want.
	for i = #spy.log, 1, -1 do
		if #out >= limit then break end
		out[#out + 1] = spy.log[i]
	end
	return { ok = true, spyId = p.spyId, calls = spy.calls, logged = #spy.log, returned = #out, entries = out }
end

local function closureSpy(p)
	local action = tostring(p.action or "")
	if action == "start" then return spyStart(p) end
	if action == "stop" then return spyStop(p) end
	if action == "list" then return spyList() end
	if action == "logs" then return spyLogs(p) end
	return { ok = false, error = 'action must be "start", "stop", "list" or "logs"' }
end
-- Real MCP namecall broker: ONE __namecall hook for the whole MCP, with subscribers on top.
--
-- Why a broker rather than a hook per tool: remote-spy, spy-namecall and live-reload's
-- STATE.namecallHook each installed their own hookmetamethod(game, "__namecall", ...). Three
-- independent installs on a single metamethod cannot be undone independently - restoring one puts the
-- engine's original back and silently drops the others out of the chain, while their own `installed`
-- flags keep reporting healthy and their logs just go quiet. One owner removes that by construction.
--
-- The cost floor matters more than anything else in this file. This function runs on EVERY :Method()
-- call in the game - FindFirstChild, IsA, Clone, part methods, thousands per frame - so nothing is
-- allocated until a subscriber has actually matched the method name. The version this replaces
-- allocated a table AND a closure per namecall before it even read the method name, which is what
-- made games unplayable while a spy was installed.
--
-- Three guarantees the individual hooks did not have:
--   * DataModel identity. A game change destroys the hook but not the getgenv state, so a surviving
--     `installed` flag used to mean "reports healthy, intercepts nothing". The registry remembers
--     which DataModel it installed into and reinstalls when that is no longer the current one.
--   * Liveness. `seen` counts every game-originated namecall, before any filter. seen climbing with
--     nothing logged means the filter is wrong; seen stuck at 0 means the hook is dead. Those two
--     were indistinguishable before.
--   * Self-restore. A deadline and a rate limit, so a forgotten spy stops on its own instead of
--     degrading the client until the user rejoins.

local REG_KEY = "__mcp_hookreg"

-- getgenv() does not hand back a stable table identity (see notes-getgenv-identity), so the registry
-- is resolved into a local exactly once and every reference below goes through that local.
local __genv = (getgenv and getgenv()) or _G

local __reg = __genv[REG_KEY]
if type(__reg) ~= "table" then
	__reg = {
		subs = {},        -- name -> { methods = {m=true}, on = fn, after = fn|nil, seen = 0, matched = 0 }
		methods = {},     -- method -> array of subscriber names, the hot-path lookup
		seen = 0,         -- game-originated namecalls the hook has seen, before any filter
		installed = false,
		dm = nil,         -- the DataModel the hook was installed into
		recording = true,
		deadlineAt = nil, -- os.clock() past which the broker restores itself
		windowStart = 0,  -- rate window
		windowCount = 0,
		stoppedReason = nil,
		gen = 0,
	}
	__genv[REG_KEY] = __reg
end
local REG = __reg

-- Rebuild the method -> subscribers lookup. Only ever called from register/unregister, never from the
-- hot path, so the hot path is a single table index.
local function rebuildMethods()
	local m = {}
	for name, sub in pairs(REG.subs) do
		for method in pairs(sub.methods) do
			local list = m[method]
			if not list then
				list = {}
				m[method] = list
			end
			list[#list + 1] = name
		end
	end
	REG.methods = m
end

-- How long a spy may sit untouched before the broker puts the game back the way it found it, and how
-- many intercepted calls per second are tolerated before it stops recording. Both exist because a
-- forgotten or too-broad spy is otherwise indistinguishable from a broken game.
local IDLE_RESTORE_SECONDS = 300
local RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND = 2000

local function restore()
	REG.gen = (REG.gen or 0) + 1
	REG.recording = false
	if REG.installed and typeof(REG.original) == "function" then
		pcall(hookmetamethod, game, "__namecall", REG.original)
	end
	REG.installed = false
	REG.original = nil
	REG.dm = nil
	return true
end

local function install()
	-- A surviving flag from a previous DataModel is exactly the lie this check exists to catch.
	if REG.installed and REG.dm == game then
		return true
	end
	if REG.installed and REG.dm ~= game then
		-- The old hook died with the old DataModel. Drop the stale handles and install fresh.
		REG.installed = false
		REG.original = nil
	end
	if typeof(hookmetamethod) ~= "function" or typeof(getnamecallmethod) ~= "function" or typeof(checkcaller) ~= "function" then
		REG.unavailable = true
		return false, "needs hookmetamethod, getnamecallmethod and checkcaller"
	end

	local original
	local function nc(self, ...)
		-- Our own code comes back through here; checkcaller is both the recursion guard and what keeps
		-- the hook off its own back. Nothing above this line allocates.
		if checkcaller() then
			return original(self, ...)
		end
		REG.seen = REG.seen + 1
		if not REG.recording then
			return original(self, ...)
		end
		local method = getnamecallmethod()
		local names = REG.methods[method]
		if not names then
			-- The overwhelmingly common path, and it allocates nothing.
			return original(self, ...)
		end

		-- Past this point a subscriber wants this call, so the cost is proportional to what is being
		-- watched rather than to the game's total traffic.
		local now = os.clock()
		if now - REG.windowStart >= 1 then
			REG.windowStart = now
			REG.windowCount = 0
		end
		REG.windowCount = REG.windowCount + 1
		if REG.windowCount > RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND then
			REG.recording = false
			REG.stoppedReason = "stopped recording: more than " .. RATE_LIMIT_PER_SECOND ..
				" intercepted calls per second. The filter is too broad for this game - narrow it and start again."
			return original(self, ...)
		end
		REG.deadlineAt = now + IDLE_RESTORE_SECONDS

		local a = table.pack(...)
		local blocked = false
		local substituted = false
		local subValue = nil
		local watchers = nil
		for i = 1, #names do
			local sub = REG.subs[names[i]]
			if sub then
				sub.matched = (sub.matched or 0) + 1
				-- A subscriber returns nothing to let the call through, "block" to swallow it, or
				-- "substitute", value to answer in the game's place.
				local ok, action, value = pcall(sub.on, self, method, a)
				if ok then
					if action == "block" then
						blocked = true
					elseif action == "substitute" then
						substituted = true
						subValue = value
					end
				end
				if sub.after then
					watchers = watchers or {}
					watchers[#watchers + 1] = sub
				end
			end
		end

		if substituted then
			return subValue
		end
		if blocked then
			return
		end
		-- Only pay for capturing the return when someone asked to see it. This is how remote-spy gets
		-- an InvokeServer's reply without every other call paying for a table.pack of the results.
		if watchers then
			local rets = table.pack(original(self, ...))
			for i = 1, #watchers do
				pcall(watchers[i].after, self, method, a, rets)
			end
			return table.unpack(rets, 1, rets.n)
		end
		return original(self, ...)
	end

	-- A bare Lua closure here is what crashed an earlier version: wrapped as a C closure the replaced
	-- metamethod matches the shape of the one it replaced.
	local hookFn = nc
	if typeof(newcclosure) == "function" then
		local okC, c = pcall(newcclosure, nc)
		if okC and c then
			hookFn = c
		end
	end

	local okInstall, result = pcall(hookmetamethod, game, "__namecall", hookFn)
	if not okInstall then
		REG.installError = tostring(result)
		return false, REG.installError
	end
	original = result
	REG.original = result
	REG.installed = true
	REG.dm = game
	REG.installError = nil
	REG.recording = true
	REG.stoppedReason = nil
	REG.deadlineAt = os.clock() + IDLE_RESTORE_SECONDS

	-- The watchdog lives off the hot path on purpose: checking a deadline inside the hook would pay a
	-- clock read per intercepted call for something that only needs to be true within a second.
	REG.gen = (REG.gen or 0) + 1
	local myGen = REG.gen
	task.spawn(function()
		while REG.gen == myGen and REG.installed do
			if REG.deadlineAt and os.clock() > REG.deadlineAt then
				REG.stoppedReason = "restored automatically after " .. IDLE_RESTORE_SECONDS ..
					"s without a check. Start the spy again if you still need it."
				restore()
				return
			end
			task.wait(1)
		end
	end)
	return true
end

-- Register a subscriber. `methods` is an array of method names; `on(self, method, argsPacked)` may
-- return "block"; `after(self, method, argsPacked, retsPacked)` is optional and only installed for
-- subscribers that need to see the return value.
local function register(name, methods, on, after)
	local set = {}
	for _, m in ipairs(methods) do
		if type(m) == "string" and m ~= "" then
			set[m] = true
		end
	end
	REG.subs[name] = { methods = set, on = on, after = after, matched = 0 }
	rebuildMethods()
	local ok, err = install()
	if not ok then
		REG.subs[name] = nil
		rebuildMethods()
		return false, err
	end
	-- Touch the deadline so registering counts as activity.
	REG.deadlineAt = os.clock() + IDLE_RESTORE_SECONDS
	REG.recording = true
	REG.stoppedReason = nil
	return true
end

local function unregister(name)
	REG.subs[name] = nil
	rebuildMethods()
	-- Nothing left to watch: put the game back rather than leaving a pass-through hook in place.
	if next(REG.subs) == nil then
		restore()
	end
	return true
end

-- Refresh the idle deadline. Every read operation calls this, so a spy that is being watched stays,
-- and one that is forgotten does not.
local function touch()
	if REG.installed then
		REG.deadlineAt = os.clock() + IDLE_RESTORE_SECONDS
	end
end

local function status(name)
	local sub = name and REG.subs[name] or nil
	return {
		installed = REG.installed == true,
		recording = REG.recording == true,
		-- seen is the liveness proof: climbing with nothing logged means the filter is wrong, stuck at
		-- zero means the hook is not intercepting at all.
		seen = REG.seen or 0,
		matched = sub and (sub.matched or 0) or nil,
		subscribers = (function()
			local names = {}
			for n in pairs(REG.subs) do
				names[#names + 1] = n
			end
			return names
		end)(),
		stoppedReason = REG.stoppedReason,
		installError = REG.installError,
		idleRestoreSeconds = IDLE_RESTORE_SECONDS,
	}
end

local __hookreg = {
	register = register,
	unregister = unregister,
	restore = restore,
	touch = touch,
	status = status,
	reg = REG,
}

-- STATE.namecallHook(method, fn) installs ONE __namecall hook for the whole session and routes each
-- method to the handler registered for it. Doing this by hand in a reloaded script is the most
-- common way to wedge a client: a bare Lua closure where a C closure belonged, a re-run stacking a
-- second hook whose upvalues point at the dead previous generation, and no guard against the hook
-- re-entering itself. Here the hook is installed once, handlers live in a table this reload replaces,
-- and a handler is dropped on cleanup like any other registration.
-- fn(self, method, ...) may return a value to substitute the call's result; return nothing to let
-- the original run.
-- Routed through the MCP's shared namecall broker rather than installing a hook of its own. Three
-- separate installs on one metamethod could not be undone independently: restoring any one of them
-- put the engine's original back and silently dropped the others, which then kept reporting healthy
-- while intercepting nothing. The broker also means this costs nothing on the methods it does not
-- watch, and that a forgotten hook restores itself.
__slot.namecallHook = function(method, fn)
	if type(method) ~= "string" or type(fn) ~= "function" then return false end
	local subName = "live:__LIVE_LABEL__:" .. method
	local ok = __hookreg.register(subName, { method }, function(self, m, a)
		local okCall, r = pcall(fn, self, m, table.unpack(a, 1, a.n))
		-- Same contract as before: return a value to substitute the call's result, return nothing to
		-- let the original run.
		if okCall and r ~= nil then return "substitute", r end
		return nil
	end, nil)
	table.insert(__slot.__cleanup, function() __hookreg.unregister(subName) end)
	return ok
end
-- STATE.override(tbl, key, value) replaces a field and puts the old one back on the next reload.
--
-- Reassigning a module's field - CameraController.Recoil, a GetFireDirection - is one of the most
-- common ways to change a game's behaviour, and it was the one thing a reload could not undo:
-- onCleanup handles connections and hooks, but a plain assignment left the previous run's function
-- in place, so a second reload saved the ALREADY overridden function as the original and the real
-- one was gone for the rest of the session. Everyone hit this and everyone hand-rolled the same
-- getgenv cache to work around it.
--
-- The DataModel is recorded with each saved original, and a restore into a different one is refused.
-- That is the other half of the same bug: after a rejoin the cached original is a function from the
-- dead session, and putting it back into the new game's module is worse than not restoring at all -
-- it swaps live code for something that closed over a client that no longer exists.
__slot.override = function(tbl, key, value)
	if type(tbl) ~= "table" and typeof(tbl) ~= "Instance" then return false end
	local ok, previous = pcall(function() return tbl[key] end)
	if not ok then return false end
	local dm = game
	if not pcall(function() tbl[key] = value end) then return false end
	table.insert(__slot.__cleanup, function()
		if game ~= dm then return end
		pcall(function() tbl[key] = previous end)
	end)
	return true
end
__genv.STATE = __slot

-- globally could see a different table than the one this prelude just prepared - which made
-- STATE.alive() report the previous generation. As a local it is captured as an upvalue by the
-- body closure below, so there is exactly one authoritative reference. The global assignment above
-- stays as a convenience for code that goes looking for getgenv().STATE.
local STATE = __slot

__LIVE_LABEL__
end
local __liveOk, __liveErr = pcall(__liveBody)
if not __liveOk then error(__liveErr, 0) end

¿¿¿␀-- Real MCP watch-value: sample a Luau expression over a window and report how it changed over time,
-- so a caller can tell whether a value it wrote sticks or the server resets it on a later tick,
-- rather than reading once and guessing. Self-contained: the expression is compiled from a params
-- string, so nothing is inlined into this chunk.
local function runWatch()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local expr = p.expression
	if type(expr) ~= "string" or expr == "" then
		return { error = "expression is required" }
	end
	local durationMs = tonumber(p.durationMs) or 3000
	if durationMs > 30000 then durationMs = 30000 end
	if durationMs < 100 then durationMs = 100 end
	local intervalMs = tonumber(p.intervalMs) or 100
	if intervalMs < 20 then intervalMs = 20 end
	if intervalMs > 5000 then intervalMs = 5000 end

	-- Compile separately from this chunk, so a bad expression is a clean error rather than a silent
	-- failure of the whole payload. Real's executor exposes loadstring, not the standard load.
	--
	-- The newlines matter: wrapping inline as `return (expr)` let a trailing `-- comment` swallow the
	-- closing paren and report "Expected 'end'". And if the expression form does not compile at all,
	-- the caller sent statements, which are run as-is so their own return decides the value.
	local fn, err = loadstring("return (\n" .. expr .. "\n)", "watch-value")
	if not fn then
		fn = loadstring(expr, "watch-value")
	end
	if not fn then
		return { error = "could not compile expression: " .. tostring(err) }
	end

	-- A cheap signature to detect change without deep-comparing tables. Primitives compare by value;
	-- Instances, Vector3, CFrame etc. compare by their tostring, which is enough to notice a move.
	local function sig(ok, v)
		if not ok then return "error:" .. tostring(v) end
		return typeof(v) .. ":" .. tostring(v)
	end

	local samples = {}
	local lastSig = nil
	local total = 0
	local elapsed = 0
	local budget = durationMs / 1000
	-- Accumulate the real time task.wait actually slept, so the window is wall-clock and does not
	-- depend on os.clock's meaning in the executor.
	while elapsed < budget do
		local ok, v = pcall(fn)
		local s = sig(ok, v)
		if s ~= lastSig then
			lastSig = s
			local entry = { tMs = math.floor(elapsed * 1000 + 0.5) }
			if ok then
				entry.value = v
			else
				entry.error = tostring(v)
			end
			samples[#samples + 1] = entry
		end
		total = total + 1
		elapsed = elapsed + task.wait(intervalMs / 1000)
	end

	local first = samples[1]
	local last = samples[#samples]
	return {
		expression = expr,
		sampledForMs = durationMs,
		intervalMs = intervalMs,
		totalSamples = total,
		-- samples holds one entry per CHANGE (the first reading included), so changes is one fewer.
		changes = math.max(0, #samples - 1),
		changed = #samples > 1,
		firstValue = first and first.value,
		lastValue = last and last.value,
		samples = samples,
	}
end

return runWatch()
-- Real MCP memory introspection. Scans the Luau GC via filtergc and dumps environment tables
-- (getgenv/getrenv/getreg), with paging and bounded previews. Runs inside the action runtime, so
-- safe and __MCP are visible. Read only: no setupvalue/setconstant/setstack here.

local dbg = debug or {}
local fnGetInfo = getinfo or dbg.getinfo
local fnGetUpvalues = getupvalues or dbg.getupvalues
local fnGetConstants = getconstants or dbg.getconstants

-- Only forward filter fields the caller actually set, so an omitted field is no constraint.
local function buildTableFilter(p)
	local f = {}
	if type(p.keys) == "table" and #p.keys > 0 then f.Keys = p.keys end
	if type(p.values) == "table" and #p.values > 0 then f.Values = p.values end
	return f
end

local function buildFunctionFilter(p)
	local f = {}
	if type(p.name) == "string" and p.name ~= "" then f.Name = p.name end
	if type(p.constants) == "table" and #p.constants > 0 then f.Constants = p.constants end
	if type(p.upvalues) == "table" and #p.upvalues > 0 then f.Upvalues = p.upvalues end
	-- Skip the executor's own closures by default, they otherwise flood every result.
	if p.ignoreExecutor ~= false then f.IgnoreExecutor = true end
	return f
end

local function gcScan(p)
	if typeof(filtergc) ~= "function" then
		return { error = "filtergc is not available in this executor" }
	end
	local kind = (p.kind == "function") and "function" or "table"
	local offset = math.max(0, tonumber(p.offset) or 0)
	local limit = math.max(1, math.min(tonumber(p.limit) or 20, 100))
	local filter = (kind == "function") and buildFunctionFilter(p) or buildTableFilter(p)

	-- filtergc does the native filtering; we only serialize the requested page.
	local ok, matches = pcall(filtergc, kind, filter, false)
	if not ok then
		return { error = "filtergc failed: " .. tostring(matches) }
	end
	if type(matches) ~= "table" then matches = {} end

	local total = #matches
	local stop = math.min(total, offset + limit)
	local out = {}
	for i = offset + 1, stop do
		local item = matches[i]
		if kind == "table" then
			out[#out + 1] = { id = tostring(item), value = item }
		else
			local entry = { id = tostring(item) }
			if typeof(fnGetInfo) == "function" then
				local okInfo, info = pcall(fnGetInfo, item)
				if okInfo then entry.info = info end
			end
			if p.includeUpvalues then
				if typeof(fnGetUpvalues) == "function" then
					local okU, ups = pcall(fnGetUpvalues, item)
					if okU then entry.upvalues = ups end
				end
				if typeof(fnGetConstants) == "function" then
					local okC, consts = pcall(fnGetConstants, item)
					if okC then entry.constants = consts end
				end
			end
			out[#out + 1] = entry
		end
	end

	return {
		kind = kind,
		total = total,
		offset = offset,
		returned = #out,
		hasMore = stop < total,
		matches = out,
	}
end

-- Compact per entry preview so one giant global cannot eat the whole output budget.
local function previewValue(v)
	local t = typeof(v)
	if t == "table" then
		local n = 0
		for _ in pairs(v) do
			n += 1
			if n >= 500 then break end
		end
		return { __t = "table", approxKeys = n, id = tostring(v) }
	elseif t == "function" then
		return "<function>"
	elseif t == "Instance" then
		return { __t = "Instance", ClassName = v.ClassName, Name = v.Name }
	elseif t == "string" then
		if #v > 200 then return string.sub(v, 1, 200) .. "..." end
		return v
	elseif t == "number" or t == "boolean" then
		return v
	end
	return tostring(v)
end

local function envDump(p)
	local which = p.which
	local getter
	if which == "renv" then
		getter = getrenv
	elseif which == "reg" then
		getter = getreg or getregistry
	else
		which = "genv"
		getter = getgenv
	end
	if typeof(getter) ~= "function" then
		return { error = "environment getter not available: " .. tostring(which) }
	end
	local ok, env = pcall(getter)
	if not ok or type(env) ~= "table" then
		return { error = "failed to read environment: " .. tostring(which) }
	end

	local keyContains = (type(p.keyContains) == "string" and p.keyContains ~= "") and p.keyContains or nil
	local offset = math.max(0, tonumber(p.offset) or 0)
	local limit = math.max(1, math.min(tonumber(p.limit) or 40, 200))

	-- Capture values during iteration (registry keys can be non string, so no re-lookup by name).
	local entries = {}
	local capped = false
	for k, v in pairs(env) do
		local ks = tostring(k)
		if (not keyContains) or string.find(ks, keyContains, 1, true) then
			entries[#entries + 1] = { key = ks, value = v }
			if #entries >= 4000 then
				capped = true
				break
			end
		end
	end
	table.sort(entries, function(a, b) return a.key < b.key end)

	local total = #entries
	local stop = math.min(total, offset + limit)
	local out = {}
	for i = offset + 1, stop do
		local e = entries[i]
		out[#out + 1] = { key = e.key, type = typeof(e.value), preview = previewValue(e.value) }
	end

	return {
		which = which,
		total = total,
		scanTruncated = capped,
		offset = offset,
		returned = #out,
		hasMore = stop < total,
		entries = out,
	}
end
-- Real MCP session recorder: one window that captures remote traffic AND samples expressions, on one
-- timeline. Depends on the serializer local (safe) and the namecall broker (__hookreg).
--
-- The problem it solves is not technical. Testing a change meant asking the user to do something and
-- report back, once per attempt, because nothing could observe an action and its effect together -
-- over twenty rounds went that way in one session. With both on a single clock, one round answers
-- what several used to: fire once, and the recording shows which remotes went out, what came back,
-- and how the watched values moved around them.
--
-- Everything is timestamped from one clock read at the start, so the ordering between a remote call
-- and a value change is meaningful rather than approximate.

local function runRecord()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local durationMs = tonumber(p.durationMs) or 6000
	if durationMs > 60000 then durationMs = 60000 end
	if durationMs < 500 then durationMs = 500 end
	local intervalMs = tonumber(p.intervalMs) or 100
	if intervalMs < 20 then intervalMs = 20 end
	if intervalMs > 2000 then intervalMs = 2000 end
	local cap = tonumber(p.cap) or 300
	if cap > 1000 then cap = 1000 end
	local nameFilter = type(p.remoteName) == "string" and p.remoteName ~= "" and p.remoteName or nil

	-- Compile each watched expression once. A bad one is reported and skipped rather than taking the
	-- whole recording down with it.
	local watches = {}
	if type(p.watch) == "table" then
		for _, item in ipairs(p.watch) do
			if type(item) == "string" and item ~= "" then
				local fn, err = loadstring("return (\n" .. item .. "\n)", "record-watch")
				if fn then
					watches[#watches + 1] = { expr = item, fn = fn, last = nil, samples = {} }
				else
					watches[#watches + 1] = { expr = item, error = "did not compile: " .. tostring(err) }
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local t0 = os.clock()
	local function stamp()
		return math.floor((os.clock() - t0) * 1000 + 0.5)
	end

	local events = {}
	local SUB = "record"
	local dropped = 0

	local function onCall(self, method, a)
		if #events >= cap then
			dropped = dropped + 1
			return nil
		end
		local okN, name = pcall(function() return self.Name end)
		if not okN then return nil end
		if nameFilter and not string.find(name, nameFilter, 1, true) then
			return nil
		end
		local entry = { tMs = stamp(), kind = "remote", name = name, method = method }
		local okP, full = pcall(function() return self:GetFullName() end)
		entry.path = okP and full or nil
		local vals = {}
		for i = 1, a.n do vals[i] = a[i] end
		local okS, sc = pcall(safe, vals)
		entry.args = okS and sc or "<args unserializable>"
		events[#events + 1] = entry
		return nil
	end

	local hooked = false
	if p.recordRemotes ~= false then
		local ok = __hookreg.register(SUB, { "FireServer", "InvokeServer" }, onCall, nil)
		hooked = ok == true
	end

	-- Sample on the same clock as the events, recording only CHANGES so a value that sits still costs
	-- one entry rather than one per tick.
	local waited = 0
	local budget = durationMs / 1000
	while waited < budget do
		for _, w in ipairs(watches) do
			if w.fn then
				local ok, v = pcall(w.fn)
				local sig = ok and (typeof(v) .. ":" .. tostring(v)) or ("error:" .. tostring(v))
				if sig ~= w.last then
					w.last = sig
					local rec = { tMs = stamp() }
					if ok then rec.value = v else rec.error = tostring(v) end
					if #w.samples < cap then
						w.samples[#w.samples + 1] = rec
					end
				end
			end
		end
		waited = waited + task.wait(intervalMs / 1000)
	end

	if hooked then
		__hookreg.unregister(SUB)
	end

	local out = {}
	for _, w in ipairs(watches) do
		local serialised = {}
		for i, rec in ipairs(w.samples or {}) do
			local okS, sv = pcall(safe, rec.value)
			serialised[i] = { tMs = rec.tMs, value = okS and sv or nil, error = rec.error }
		end
		out[#out + 1] = {
			expression = w.expr,
			error = w.error,
			changes = math.max(0, #serialised - 1),
			samples = serialised,
		}
	end

	return {
		recordedForMs = math.floor(waited * 1000 + 0.5),
		intervalMs = intervalMs,
		remotesRecorded = hooked,
		remoteEvents = events,
		eventCount = #events,
		droppedAfterCap = dropped,
		watches = out,
		note = "tMs on every entry is milliseconds from the start of the recording, on one clock, so remote calls and value changes can be read against each other.",
	}
end

return runRecord()
