␀-- Real MCP frame profiler: measure what the client's frame rate is doing, so the cost of a script
-- that runs every frame is visible BEFORE it is left running. An expensive per-frame body (a heap
-- walk, an unbounded descendant scan) drops the game to single-digit FPS, and until now the only way
-- to find that out was to ship it and have the user complain.
--
-- Two modes. With no code, it samples the running client as it is - the baseline, or the cost of
-- whatever is already loaded. With code, it measures the baseline first, then runs the code every
-- frame for the same window and reports both, so the difference is attributable.
local function runProfile()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local durationMs = tonumber(p.durationMs) or 2000
	if durationMs > 15000 then durationMs = 15000 end
	if durationMs < 200 then durationMs = 200 end
	local budget = durationMs / 1000

	local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

	-- Sample frame deltas over `seconds`, optionally calling `fn` once per frame. Returns the stats
	-- for that window. Uses Heartbeat's own delta rather than a clock difference, so the numbers are
	-- the frame times the engine actually saw.
	local function sample(seconds, fn)
		local frames, total, worst = 0, 0, 0
		local slow = 0
		local conn
		conn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
			frames = frames + 1
			total = total + dt
			if dt > worst then worst = dt end
			-- Anything past ~33ms is a frame the user can feel.
			if dt > 0.033 then slow = slow + 1 end
			if fn then pcall(fn, dt) end
		end)
		local waited = 0
		while waited < seconds do
			waited = waited + task.wait()
		end
		pcall(function() conn:Disconnect() end)
		local avg = frames > 0 and (total / frames) or 0
		return {
			frames = frames,
			fps = avg > 0 and math.floor(1 / avg + 0.5) or 0,
			avgFrameMs = math.floor(avg * 1000 * 100 + 0.5) / 100,
			worstFrameMs = math.floor(worst * 1000 * 100 + 0.5) / 100,
			slowFrames = slow,
		}
	end

	local baseline = sample(budget, nil)

	local code = p.code
	if type(code) ~= "string" or code == "" then
		return {
			mode = "baseline",
			sampledForMs = durationMs,
			baseline = baseline,
			note = "Frame stats for the client as it is now. Pass code to measure what running it every frame costs on top of this.",
		}
	end

	local fn, err = loadstring(code, "profile-script")
	if not fn then
		return { error = "could not compile code: " .. tostring(err) }
	end

	-- Let the client settle between the two windows so the first does not bleed into the second.
	task.wait(0.1)
	local errors = 0
	local firstError = nil
	local withCode = sample(budget, function()
		local ok, e = pcall(fn)
		if not ok then
			errors = errors + 1
			if not firstError then firstError = tostring(e) end
		end
	end)

	local costMs = math.floor((withCode.avgFrameMs - baseline.avgFrameMs) * 100 + 0.5) / 100
	local verdict
	if errors > 0 and errors >= withCode.frames then
		verdict = "The code errored on every frame, so these numbers measure the error path, not the work."
	elseif costMs >= 8 then
		verdict = "Too expensive to run every frame - this alone costs most of a frame budget. Do the work on a timer, cache it, or bound it."
	elseif costMs >= 2 then
		verdict = "Noticeable per-frame cost. Fine occasionally, questionable every frame."
	else
		verdict = "Cheap enough to run every frame."
	end

	return {
		mode = "compare",
		sampledForMs = durationMs,
		baseline = baseline,
		withCode = withCode,
		addedFrameMs = costMs,
		fpsDelta = withCode.fps - baseline.fps,
		errors = errors,
		firstError = firstError,
		verdict = verdict,
	}
end

return runProfile()
-- Real MCP bytecode access: hand a script's compiled bytecode back to the host, base64 encoded so
-- it survives the JSON result channel. The host parses it; nothing is decoded here.
-- Depends on resolveInstance from the instances snippet, concatenated before this one.

local function scriptBytecode(p)
	if typeof(getscriptbytecode) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "getscriptbytecode is not available in this executor" }
	end
	local encoder = base64_encode or base64encode
	if typeof(encoder) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "base64_encode is not available in this executor" }
	end

	local inst, __rerr = resolveInstance(p.path)
	if not inst then
		return { ok = false, error = __rerr or ("not found: " .. tostring(p.path)) }
	end
	local okIsA, isScript = pcall(function()
		return inst:IsA("LuaSourceContainer")
	end)
	if not (okIsA and isScript) then
		return {
			ok = false,
			error = tostring(p.path) .. " is a " .. tostring(inst.ClassName) .. ", not a script",
		}
	end

	local okBytecode, bytecode = pcall(getscriptbytecode, inst)
	if not okBytecode or type(bytecode) ~= "string" or #bytecode == 0 then
		return {
			ok = false,
			error = "could not read bytecode: " .. tostring(bytecode),
			path = inst:GetFullName(),
		}
	end

	local okEncoded, encoded = pcall(encoder, bytecode)
	if not okEncoded then
		return { ok = false, error = "base64 encoding failed: " .. tostring(encoded) }
	end

	return {
		ok = true,
		path = inst:GetFullName(),
		className = inst.ClassName,
		bytes = #bytecode,
		bytecodeBase64 = encoded,
	}
end
-- Real MCP namecall spy: logs every method call the game makes, filtered by method name and class.
-- remote-spy covers FireServer/InvokeServer specifically; this is the general case (Raycast,
-- TakeDamage, a custom method on any instance).
--
-- The hook itself lives in _hookreg.luau, which is concatenated above and owns the metamethod for the
-- whole MCP. This file only decides what to keep. Before that split this file installed its own
-- __namecall, and its `restore` put the engine's original back - silently unhooking remote-spy, which
-- went on reporting `installed = true` and returning nothing.

local SUB = "spy-namecall"

local function buf()
	local b = getgenv().__mcp_namecall
	if type(b) ~= "table" then
		b = { calls = {}, cap = 300, seq = 0, methods = {}, className = nil, excludeExecutor = false }
		getgenv().__mcp_namecall = b
	end
	return b
end

local function onCall(self, method, a)
	local b = buf()
	if b.className then
		local okC, isA = pcall(function() return self:IsA(b.className) end)
		if not (okC and isA) then
			return nil
		end
	end
	-- checkcaller (in the broker) keeps the logger off its own back, but it does not reliably catch
	-- executor code running inside a signal connection, so hooking a common method like Raycast can end
	-- up watching the caller's own script. Game code has a calling script, executor code does not.
	local okS, cs = pcall(getcallingscript)
	local callerScript = okS and cs or nil
	if b.excludeExecutor and not callerScript then
		return nil
	end

	local entry = { method = method, t = os.clock() }
	local okN, cn = pcall(function() return self.ClassName end)
	entry.class = okN and cn or nil
	local okP, full = pcall(function() return self:GetFullName() end)
	entry.path = okP and full or nil
	local vals = {}
	for i = 1, a.n do
		vals[i] = a[i]
	end
	local okA, sc = pcall(safe, vals)
	entry.args = okA and sc or "<args unserializable>"
	if callerScript then
		local okF, f = pcall(function() return callerScript:GetFullName() end)
		entry.script = okF and f or nil
	end
	b.seq = (b.seq or 0) + 1
	entry.seq = b.seq
	b.calls[#b.calls + 1] = entry
	while #b.calls > b.cap do
		table.remove(b.calls, 1)
	end
	return nil
end

local function runNamecall()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local op = p.operation or "list"
	local b = buf()

	if op == "stop" or op == "restore" then
		__hookreg.unregister(SUB)
		return {
			ok = true,
			recording = false,
			note = "Unregistered. If nothing else is watching, the game's original __namecall is back in place.",
		}
	end

	if op == "clear" then
		b.calls = {}
		return { ok = true, cleared = true, nextSince = b.seq or 0 }
	end

	if op == "list" then
		__hookreg.touch()
		local st = __hookreg.status(SUB)
		local limit = tonumber(p.limit) or 20
		local since = tonumber(p.since)
		local out = {}
		for i = #b.calls, 1, -1 do
			local e = b.calls[i]
			if not since or (type(e.seq) == "number" and e.seq > since) then
				out[#out + 1] = e
				if #out >= limit then break end
			end
		end
		return {
			ok = true,
			installed = st.installed,
			recording = st.recording,
			-- seen counts every game namecall the broker saw, before any filter; matched counts the ones
			-- that reached this spy. seen climbing with matched at 0 means the method name is wrong, not
			-- that the game is idle. Those two used to be indistinguishable.
			seen = st.seen,
			matched = st.matched,
			count = #out,
			total = #b.calls,
			nextSince = b.seq or 0,
			stoppedReason = st.stoppedReason,
			calls = out,
		}
	end

	-- start
	local wanted = {}
	if type(p.methods) == "table" then
		for _, m in ipairs(p.methods) do
			if type(m) == "string" and m ~= "" then
				wanted[#wanted + 1] = m
			end
		end
	end
	if #wanted == 0 then
		return { ok = false, error = "start needs at least one method name to log, e.g. methods = {\"Raycast\"}" }
	end
	b.methods = wanted
	b.className = type(p.className) == "string" and p.className ~= "" and p.className or nil
	b.excludeExecutor = p.excludeExecutor == true
	b.cap = tonumber(p.cap) or b.cap or 300
	b.calls = {}

	local ok, err = __hookreg.register(SUB, wanted, onCall, nil)
	if not ok then
		return { ok = false, error = "the __namecall hook could not be installed: " .. tostring(err) }
	end
	local st = __hookreg.status(SUB)
	return {
		ok = true,
		recording = true,
		installed = st.installed,
		methods = wanted,
		nextSince = b.seq or 0,
		note = "Watching. Trigger the action in game, then call list. Call stop when done - it also restores automatically after a few minutes without a check.",
	}
end

return runNamecall()
-- Real MCP hook check: answers "is this actually hooked, and by whom" without installing anything.
--
-- This exists because of a specific failure: a hook that catches nothing looks exactly like a channel
-- that carries nothing. A session concluded a remote was idle when in fact the hook had never been
-- installed, and another concluded a method was never called when the hook had been silently unhooked
-- by a different tool. Both cost rounds of testing against wrong assumptions.
--
-- Read-only by design. It installs nothing, so it is safe to call at any point, including before
-- deciding whether hooking is worth the risk at all.

local function checkHook()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local out = { ok = true }

	-- What the MCP itself currently has installed. This is the first thing to know, because an
	-- installed namecall hook is the most likely explanation for a game behaving oddly.
	local genv = (getgenv and getgenv()) or _G
	local reg = genv.__mcp_hookreg
	if type(reg) == "table" then
		local subs = {}
		for name, sub in pairs(reg.subs or {}) do
			local methods = {}
			for m in pairs(sub.methods or {}) do methods[#methods + 1] = m end
			subs[#subs + 1] = { name = name, methods = methods, matched = sub.matched or 0 }
		end
		out.mcpNamecall = {
			installed = reg.installed == true,
			recording = reg.recording == true,
			-- Every game namecall the broker saw. Zero here with a subscriber registered means the
			-- hook is not intercepting at all, which is a different problem from a wrong filter.
			seen = reg.seen or 0,
			subscribers = subs,
			stoppedReason = reg.stoppedReason,
			-- The hook dies with the DataModel, so state left over from a previous game would report
			-- coverage that no longer exists.
			staleFromPreviousGame = reg.installed == true and reg.dm ~= game,
		}
	else
		out.mcpNamecall = { installed = false }
	end

	local inbound = genv.__mcp_inbound
	if type(inbound) == "table" then
		local n = 0
		for _ in pairs(inbound.hooks or {}) do n = n + 1 end
		out.mcpInbound = { listenersHooked = n, seen = inbound.seen or 0, staleFromPreviousGame = n > 0 and inbound.dm ~= game }
	end

	local spies = genv.__real_spies
	if type(spies) == "table" then
		local list = {}
		for id, spy in pairs(spies) do
			list[#list + 1] = { spyId = id, label = spy.label, calls = spy.calls or 0, logged = spy.log and #spy.log or 0 }
		end
		if #list > 0 then out.mcpClosureSpies = list end
	end

	-- Optionally answer the question about one specific function.
	local getter = p.getter
	if type(getter) == "string" and getter ~= "" then
		local chunk, compileErr = loadstring("return (\n" .. getter .. "\n)", "check-hook-getter")
		if not chunk then
			out.target = { error = "getter did not compile: " .. tostring(compileErr) }
			return out
		end
		local okRun, target = pcall(chunk)
		if not okRun then
			out.target = { error = "getter errored: " .. tostring(target) }
			return out
		end
		if type(target) ~= "function" then
			out.target = { error = "getter resolved to " .. typeof(target) .. ", not a function. Nothing can be hooked but a function." }
			return out
		end
		local info = { resolved = true }
		if typeof(isfunctionhooked) == "function" then
			local okH, h = pcall(isfunctionhooked, target)
			info.hooked = okH and h or nil
		end
		if typeof(getfunctionhash) == "function" then
			local okS, sh = pcall(getfunctionhash, target)
			-- nil for a C function, which is itself worth knowing: those behave differently under
			-- hookfunction than Lua closures do.
			info.bytecodeHash = okS and sh or nil
			info.isLuaClosure = okS and sh ~= nil or nil
		end
		if typeof(iscclosure) == "function" then
			local okC, c = pcall(iscclosure, target)
			info.isCClosure = okC and c or nil
		end
		info.note = info.hooked == true
			and "This function currently has a hook on it. If it is not yours, the game or an anticheat put it there."
			or "No hook on this function right now. If you expected one, it was never installed or something removed it - do not read an empty log as an idle target."
		out.target = info
	end

	return out
end

return checkHook()
-- Real MCP instance helpers: resolve an instance by path, walk descendants with a QueryDescendants
-- subset selector, and build a bounded descendants tree. Declared inside the action body so they
-- share scope with the tool logic that calls them.

local __cs = game:GetService("CollectionService")

-- Returns the instance, or (nil, reason). The reason names the last element that DID resolve and the
-- child that did not, so a caller learns "'CharacterCollisions' has no child 'madsheedy7'" instead
-- of a bare "not found" for the whole path - which reads like a wrong prefix and sends the caller
-- chasing game./workspace variants when the real problem is one missing child. Leading game/workspace
-- are already optional here; the prefix is never the cause.
local function resolveInstance(path)
	if not path or path == "" or path == "game" or path == "DataModel" then
		return game
	end
	-- Split into dot-separated parts up front, so a part that does not resolve can greedily absorb
	-- the parts after it: a child whose own name contains a dot (e.g. "ServerDamage.routeschema", the
	-- naming a buffer-networking framework uses) would otherwise be split apart and never found.
	local parts = {}
	for part in string.gmatch(path, "[^%.]+") do parts[#parts + 1] = part end
	local current = game
	local walked = "game"
	local i = 1
	while i <= #parts do
		local part = parts[i]
		if part == "game" then
			current = game
			walked = "game"
			i = i + 1
		elseif part == "workspace" or part == "Workspace" then
			current = workspace
			walked = "Workspace"
			i = i + 1
		else
			local nextInst = current:FindFirstChild(part)
			if not nextInst then
				local ok, svc = pcall(function() return game:GetService(part) end)
				if ok and svc then nextInst = svc end
			end
			if not nextInst then
				-- property fallback so LocalPlayer, Character, Parent, PrimaryPart etc. resolve
				local ok, v = pcall(function() return current[part] end)
				if ok and typeof(v) == "Instance" then nextInst = v end
			end
			local consumed = 1
			if not nextInst then
				-- The child's own name may contain dots. Rejoin the following parts one at a time and
				-- look for a single child by that combined name, shortest match first.
				local combined = part
				for j = i + 1, #parts do
					combined = combined .. "." .. parts[j]
					local hit = current:FindFirstChild(combined)
					if hit then
						nextInst = hit
						consumed = j - i + 1
						break
					end
				end
			end
			if not nextInst then
				return nil, "'" .. walked .. "' resolved, but it has no child, service or property named '" .. part .. "'"
			end
			current = nextInst
			walked = parts[i + consumed - 1]
			i = i + consumed
		end
	end
	return current
end

-- Build a matcher for a single selector token: ClassName, #Name, .Tag, [Prop=Value], [$Attr].
local function tokenMatcher(token)
	token = token:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")
	local first = token:sub(1, 1)
	if first == "#" then
		local name = token:sub(2)
		return function(inst) return inst.Name == name end
	elseif first == "." then
		local tag = token:sub(2)
		return function(inst) return __cs:HasTag(inst, tag) end
	elseif first == "[" then
		local inner = token:sub(2, -2)
		local key, val = inner:match("^([%w_]+)=(.+)$")
		if key then
			return function(inst)
				local ok, v = pcall(function() return inst[key] end)
				return ok and tostring(v) == val
			end
		end
		local akey = inner:match("^%$([%w_]+)$")
		if akey then
			return function(inst) return inst:GetAttribute(akey) ~= nil end
		end
		return function() return false end
	else
		return function(inst)
			local ok, isa = pcall(function() return inst:IsA(token) end)
			if ok and isa then return true end
			return inst.ClassName == token
		end
	end
end

local function describeMatch(inst)
	return { Name = inst.Name, ClassName = inst.ClassName, Path = inst:GetFullName() }
end

-- Roblox ships a native selector engine that understands far more than the subset implemented
-- above: :not(), :has(), the > (child) and >> (descendant) combinators, and property/attribute
-- predicates. Use it when present and keep the hand-rolled matcher purely as a fallback, so a
-- client without QueryDescendants still answers instead of erroring.
local function queryDescendants(root, selector, limit)
	local okNative, native = pcall(function()
		return root:QueryDescendants(selector)
	end)
	if okNative and typeof(native) == "table" then
		local out = {}
		for _, inst in ipairs(native) do
			if #out >= limit then break end
			out[#out + 1] = describeMatch(inst)
		end
		-- count is the engine's true total, so the caller can tell how much it did not see.
		return { count = #native, returned = #out, limited = #native > #out, results = out, engine = "native" }
	end

	local matchers = {}
	for part in string.gmatch(selector or "", "[^,]+") do
		table.insert(matchers, tokenMatcher(part))
	end
	local out = {}
	if #matchers == 0 then
		return { count = 0, returned = 0, limited = false, results = out, engine = "fallback" }
	end
	-- Keep counting past the limit so `count` stays a real total rather than stopping at `limit`.
	local total, scanned = 0, 0
	for _, inst in ipairs(root:GetDescendants()) do
		-- A large place holds six figures of descendants. Walking them without ever yielding
		-- starves the scheduler and the client looks frozen, so give it a breath periodically.
		scanned = scanned + 1
		if scanned % 2000 == 0 then task.wait() end
		for _, m in ipairs(matchers) do
			local ok, matched = pcall(m, inst)
			if ok and matched then
				total = total + 1
				if #out < limit then out[#out + 1] = describeMatch(inst) end
				break
			end
		end
	end
	return { count = total, returned = #out, limited = total > #out, results = out, engine = "fallback" }
end

local function descendantsTree(root, maxDepth, maxChildren, countsOnly)
	local budget = 300
	-- A container can hold thousands of children (one game had 5877 sound players). Naming twenty of
	-- them says nothing useful and costs a wall of output, while "{Sound = 5877}" says exactly what is
	-- in there. countsOnly reports each node's children as a class histogram instead of a list.
	local function classCounts(kids)
		local counts, distinct = {}, 0
		for _, k in ipairs(kids) do
			local okC, cn = pcall(function() return k.ClassName end)
			local key = okC and cn or "?"
			if counts[key] == nil then distinct = distinct + 1 end
			counts[key] = (counts[key] or 0) + 1
		end
		return counts, distinct
	end
	local function walk(inst, depth)
		budget = budget - 1
		local node = { Name = inst.Name, ClassName = inst.ClassName }
		if depth < maxDepth and budget > 0 then
			local kids = inst:GetChildren()
			if countsOnly then
				if #kids > 0 then
					node.ChildCount = #kids
					node.ChildClasses = (classCounts(kids))
				end
			else
				local n = math.min(#kids, maxChildren)
				local children = {}
				for i = 1, n do
					if budget <= 0 then break end
					children[i] = walk(kids[i], depth + 1)
				end
				if #children > 0 then node.Children = children end
				if #kids > n then node.More = #kids - n end
			end
		end
		return node
	end
	return walk(root, 0)
end

-- Roblox has no runtime "list all properties" call, so we probe a curated union of common property
-- names. A name that is not a member of the instance's class just fails the pcall and is skipped.
local PROP_NAMES = {
	"Archivable", "Parent",
	-- BasePart
	"Position", "Size", "Orientation", "CFrame", "Anchored", "CanCollide", "CanTouch", "CanQuery",
	"Transparency", "Reflectance", "Material", "Color", "BrickColor", "CastShadow", "CollisionGroup",
	"Massless", "RootPriority", "AssemblyLinearVelocity", "AssemblyAngularVelocity", "Shape",
	-- Model
	"PrimaryPart", "WorldPivot", "ModelStreamingMode", "Scale",
	-- Humanoid
	"Health", "MaxHealth", "WalkSpeed", "JumpPower", "JumpHeight", "UseJumpPower", "HipHeight",
	"DisplayName", "RigType", "AutoRotate", "PlatformStand", "Sit", "FloorMaterial",
	-- Player
	"UserId", "Team", "TeamColor", "Neutral", "AccountAge", "CharacterAppearanceId", "FollowUserId",
	-- GuiObject
	"Visible", "AnchorPoint", "BackgroundColor3", "BackgroundTransparency", "BorderSizePixel",
	"BorderColor3", "ZIndex", "Rotation", "ClipsDescendants", "Active", "Selectable", "LayoutOrder",
	-- Text
	"Text", "TextColor3", "TextSize", "Font", "FontFace", "TextScaled", "TextWrapped",
	"TextXAlignment", "TextYAlignment", "PlaceholderText", "RichText", "TextTransparency", "LineHeight",
	-- Image
	"Image", "ImageColor3", "ImageTransparency", "ScaleType", "ResampleMode",
	-- Value objects
	"Value",
	-- Sound
	"SoundId", "Volume", "Playing", "Looped", "TimePosition", "PlaybackSpeed", "TimeLength",
	-- Light / effects
	"Brightness", "Range", "Shadows", "Enabled",
	-- Camera
	"FieldOfView", "CameraType", "CameraSubject", "Focus",
	-- Tool
	"Grip", "CanBeDropped", "RequiresHandle", "ToolTip",
	-- Attachment
	"WorldPosition", "Axis", "SecondaryAxis",
	-- ProximityPrompt
	"ActionText", "ObjectText", "HoldDuration", "MaxActivationDistance", "RequiresLineOfSight", "KeyboardKeyCode",
	-- Constraints
	"Attachment0", "Attachment1", "Length",
	-- Script
	"RunContext", "Disabled",
	-- Misc common
	"Adornee",
}

local function instanceProperties(inst, includeHidden)
	local props = {}
	local hidden = nil
	local seen = {}
	for _, name in ipairs(PROP_NAMES) do
		if not seen[name] then
			seen[name] = true
			local ok, val = pcall(function() return inst[name] end)
			if ok and val ~= nil then
				props[name] = val
			elseif includeHidden and typeof(gethiddenproperty) == "function" then
				local okH, hv = pcall(gethiddenproperty, inst, name)
				if okH and hv ~= nil then
					hidden = hidden or {}
					hidden[name] = hv
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local attributes = nil
	local okA, attrs = pcall(function() return inst:GetAttributes() end)
	if okA and typeof(attrs) == "table" then attributes = attrs end

	local tags = nil
	local okT, tagList = pcall(function() return __cs:GetTags(inst) end)
	if okT and typeof(tagList) == "table" then tags = tagList end

	local parentPath = nil
	local okP, parent = pcall(function() return inst.Parent end)
	if okP and parent then parentPath = parent:GetFullName() end

	local childCount = 0
	local okC, kids = pcall(function() return inst:GetChildren() end)
	if okC then childCount = #kids end

	return {
		path = inst:GetFullName(),
		className = inst.ClassName,
		name = inst.Name,
		parent = parentPath,
		childrenCount = childCount,
		properties = props,
		hidden = hidden,
		attributes = attributes,
		tags = tags,
	}
end

local function taggedInstances(tag, limit)
	local out = {}
	local ok, list = pcall(function() return __cs:GetTagged(tag) end)
	if not ok or typeof(list) ~= "table" then
		return { tag = tag, count = 0, limited = false, results = out }
	end
	for _, inst in ipairs(list) do
		out[#out + 1] = { Name = inst.Name, ClassName = inst.ClassName, Path = inst:GetFullName() }
		if #out >= limit then break end
	end
	return { tag = tag, count = #out, limited = #out >= limit, results = out }
end
-- Real MCP automation helpers: decode JSON tool arguments into real Luau values, then act on the
-- game through them (fire a remote, read/write a property, call a method). Depends on
-- resolveInstance from the instances snippet, which is concatenated before this one.

-- {__instance="game.X.Y"} and the datatype wrappers become real values; anything else passes
-- through untouched.
local function toLuaValue(v)
	if type(v) == "table" then
		if v.__instance ~= nil then
			local inst, __rerr = resolveInstance(v.__instance)
			if not inst then error(__rerr or ("argument instance not found: " .. tostring(v.__instance))) end
			return inst
		end
		if type(v.__vector3) == "table" then
			return Vector3.new(v.__vector3.x or 0, v.__vector3.y or 0, v.__vector3.z or 0)
		end
		if type(v.__vector2) == "table" then
			return Vector2.new(v.__vector2.x or 0, v.__vector2.y or 0)
		end
		if type(v.__color3) == "table" then
			return Color3.new(v.__color3.r or 0, v.__color3.g or 0, v.__color3.b or 0)
		end
		if type(v.__cframe) == "table" then
			return CFrame.new(v.__cframe.x or 0, v.__cframe.y or 0, v.__cframe.z or 0)
		end
		if v.__enum ~= nil then
			local path = tostring(v.__enum):gsub("^Enum%.", "")
			local category, item = path:match("^([^%.]+)%.(.+)$")
			if category and item and Enum[category] then
				return Enum[category][item]
			end
			error("bad enum: " .. tostring(v.__enum))
		end
	end
	return v
end

-- argCount comes from the caller because JSON nulls decode to nil and would truncate the array.
local function toLuaArgs(list, argCount)
	local out = {}
	local n = argCount or 0
	if list then
		for i = 1, n do
			out[i] = toLuaValue(list[i])
		end
	end
	return out, n
end

local function memberFunction(inst, name)
	local ok, fn = pcall(function()
		return inst[name]
	end)
	if not ok or type(fn) ~= "function" then
		return nil
	end
	return fn
end

local function packReturns(packed)
	local returns = {}
	for i = 2, packed.n do
		returns[i - 1] = packed[i]
	end
	return returns
end

local function fireRemote(p)
	local remote, __rerr = resolveInstance(p.path)
	if not remote then
		return { ok = false, error = __rerr or ("not found: " .. tostring(p.path)) }
	end
	local method = p.method
	if method == nil or method == "" or method == "auto" then
		local class = remote.ClassName
		if class == "RemoteFunction" then
			method = "InvokeServer"
		elseif class == "BindableEvent" then
			method = "Fire"
		elseif class == "BindableFunction" then
			method = "Invoke"
		else
			method = "FireServer"
		end
	end
	local fn = memberFunction(remote, method)
	if not fn then
		return {
			ok = false,
			error = tostring(method) .. " is not available on " .. tostring(remote.ClassName),
		}
	end
	local args, n = toLuaArgs(p.args, p.argCount)
	local packed = table.pack(pcall(fn, remote, table.unpack(args, 1, n)))
	if not packed[1] then
		return { ok = false, error = tostring(packed[2]), method = method }
	end
	return { ok = true, path = remote:GetFullName(), method = method, returns = packReturns(packed) }
end

local function getProperty(p)
	local inst, __rerr = resolveInstance(p.path)
	if not inst then
		return { ok = false, error = __rerr or ("not found: " .. tostring(p.path)) }
	end
	local ok, value = pcall(function()
		return inst[p.property]
	end)
	if not ok then
		return { ok = false, error = tostring(value), property = p.property }
	end
	return { ok = true, path = inst:GetFullName(), property = p.property, value = value }
end

local function setProperty(p)
	local inst, __rerr = resolveInstance(p.path)
	if not inst then
		return { ok = false, error = __rerr or ("not found: " .. tostring(p.path)) }
	end
	local okv, value = pcall(toLuaValue, p.value)
	if not okv then
		return { ok = false, error = tostring(value), property = p.property }
	end
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		inst[p.property] = value
	end)
	if not ok then
		return { ok = false, error = tostring(err), property = p.property }
	end
	local after
	pcall(function()
		after = inst[p.property]
	end)
	return { ok = true, path = inst:GetFullName(), property = p.property, value = after }
end

local function callMethod(p)
	local inst, __rerr = resolveInstance(p.path)
	if not inst then
		return { ok = false, error = __rerr or ("not found: " .. tostring(p.path)) }
	end
	local fn = memberFunction(inst, p.method)
	if not fn then
		return {
			ok = false,
			error = tostring(p.method) .. " is not available on " .. tostring(inst.ClassName),
		}
	end
	local args, n = toLuaArgs(p.args, p.argCount)
	local packed = table.pack(pcall(fn, inst, table.unpack(args, 1, n)))
	if not packed[1] then
		return { ok = false, error = tostring(packed[2]), method = p.method }
	end
	return { ok = true, path = inst:GetFullName(), method = p.method, returns = packReturns(packed) }
end

-- Roster of players with the fields an agent usually needs, plus who is local.
local function listPlayers()
	local service = game:GetService("Players")
	local localPlayer
	pcall(function()
		localPlayer = service.LocalPlayer
	end)
	local roster
	local ok = pcall(function()
		roster = service:GetPlayers()
	end)
	if not ok or type(roster) ~= "table" then
		roster = {}
		for _, child in ipairs(service:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("Player") then
				roster[#roster + 1] = child
			end
		end
	end
	local list = {}
	for _, player in ipairs(roster) do
		local entry = { Name = player.Name }
		pcall(function()
			entry.DisplayName = player.DisplayName
		end)
		pcall(function()
			entry.UserId = player.UserId
		end)
		-- Team can be nil while the game keeps the real value on TeamColor, so report both.
		pcall(function()
			entry.Team = player.Team and player.Team.Name or nil
		end)
		pcall(function()
			entry.TeamColor = player.TeamColor and tostring(player.TeamColor) or nil
		end)
		pcall(function()
			entry.IsLocal = (player == localPlayer)
		end)
		pcall(function()
			local character = player.Character
			if character then
				entry.CharacterPath = character:GetFullName()
				local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
				if humanoid then
					entry.Health = humanoid.Health
					entry.MaxHealth = humanoid.MaxHealth
				end
				local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
				if root then
					entry.Position = root.Position
				end
			end
		end)
		list[#list + 1] = entry
	end
	return {
		count = #list,
		localPlayer = localPlayer and localPlayer.Name or nil,
		players = list,
	}
end
-- Real MCP runtime introspection: what actually runs when a signal fires, whether the DataModel
-- metatable has been hooked, and the instances the tree cannot reach. Depends on resolveInstance
-- from the instances snippet, which is concatenated before this one.

-- Everything we can cheaply learn about a closure without running it.
local function describeFunction(fn)
	local out = {}
	if typeof(islclosure) == "function" then
		local ok, value = pcall(islclosure, fn)
		if ok then out.IsLuaClosure = value end
	end
	if typeof(iscclosure) == "function" then
		local ok, value = pcall(iscclosure, fn)
		if ok then out.IsCClosure = value end
	end
	local okSource, source = pcall(debug.info, fn, "s")
	if okSource then out.Source = source end
	local okLine, line = pcall(debug.info, fn, "l")
	if okLine then out.Line = line end
	local okName, name = pcall(debug.info, fn, "n")
	if okName and name ~= "" then out.Name = name end
	return out
end

-- Who is listening to a signal. Answers "what runs when this button is clicked" in one call,
-- without hand-rolling a GC walk.
local function listConnections(p)
	local inst, __rerr = resolveInstance(p.path)
	if not inst then
		return { ok = false, error = __rerr or ("not found: " .. tostring(p.path)) }
	end
	if typeof(getconnections) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "getconnections is not available in this executor" }
	end
	local okSignal, signal = pcall(function()
		return inst[p.signal]
	end)
	if not okSignal or typeof(signal) ~= "RBXScriptSignal" then
		return {
			ok = false,
			error = tostring(p.signal) .. " is not a signal on " .. tostring(inst.ClassName),
		}
	end
	local okConns, conns = pcall(getconnections, signal)
	if not okConns or typeof(conns) ~= "table" then
		return { ok = false, error = "could not read connections: " .. tostring(conns) }
	end
	local limit = math.clamp(tonumber(p.limit) or 50, 1, 200)
	local out = {}
	for _, conn in ipairs(conns) do
		if #out >= limit then break end
		local entry = {}
		pcall(function() entry.Enabled = conn.Enabled end)
		pcall(function() entry.ForeignState = conn.ForeignState end)
		pcall(function() entry.LuaConnection = conn.LuaConnection end)
		local okFn, fn = pcall(function()
			return conn.Function
		end)
		if okFn and type(fn) == "function" then
			entry.Function = describeFunction(fn)
		end
		out[#out + 1] = entry
	end
	return {
		ok = true,
		path = inst:GetFullName(),
		signal = p.signal,
		count = #conns,
		returned = #out,
		limited = #conns > #out,
		connections = out,
	}
end

-- The heuristic is one line: an untouched engine metamethod is a C closure, so a Lua closure in its
-- place is somebody's hook.
local function dumpAnticheatHooks(p)
	if typeof(getrawmetatable) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "getrawmetatable is not available in this executor" }
	end
	local okMt, mt = pcall(getrawmetatable, game)
	if not okMt or type(mt) ~= "table" then
		return { ok = false, error = "could not read the DataModel metatable" }
	end
	local result = { ok = true, metamethods = {}, notes = {} }
	pcall(function()
		result.readOnly = isreadonly(mt)
	end)

	for _, name in ipairs({ "__namecall", "__index", "__newindex" }) do
		local fn = rawget(mt, name)
		local entry = { Present = fn ~= nil }
		if type(fn) == "function" then
			local info = describeFunction(fn)
			entry.IsLuaClosure = info.IsLuaClosure
			entry.IsCClosure = info.IsCClosure
			entry.Source = info.Source
			entry.Line = info.Line
			entry.Name = info.Name
			entry.LikelyHooked = info.IsLuaClosure == true
			if entry.LikelyHooked then
				result.notes[#result.notes + 1] = name
					.. " is a Lua closure, so it is hooked: "
					.. tostring(info.Source)
					.. ":"
					.. tostring(info.Line)
			end
		end
		result.metamethods[name] = entry
	end
	if #result.notes == 0 then
		result.notes[1] = "No hooked metamethod found: every present metamethod is a C closure."
	end

	-- Optional second pass: per-frame listeners whose function reports no source are loadstring'd
	-- or injected code, which is what an anti-cheat loop usually looks like.
	if p and p.scanConnections and typeof(getconnections) == "function" then
		local injected = {}
		for _, signalName in ipairs({ "Heartbeat", "Stepped", "RenderStepped" }) do
			local okSignal, signal = pcall(function()
				return game:GetService("RunService")[signalName]
			end)
			if okSignal and typeof(signal) == "RBXScriptSignal" then
				local okConns, conns = pcall(getconnections, signal)
				if okConns and typeof(conns) == "table" then
					local seen = 0
					for _, conn in ipairs(conns) do
						if seen >= 25 then break end
						seen = seen + 1
						local okFn, fn = pcall(function()
							return conn.Function
						end)
						if okFn and type(fn) == "function" then
							local info = describeFunction(fn)
							if info.Source == nil or info.Source == "" then
								injected[#injected + 1] = { Signal = signalName, Line = info.Line, Name = info.Name }
							end
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
		result.injectedConnections = injected
	end
	return result
end

-- Instances the normal tree walk cannot reach: nil-parented objects, running scripts, and Actors.
local function listSpecialInstances(p)
	local source = tostring(p.source or "nil")
	local limit = math.clamp(tonumber(p.limit) or 100, 1, 500)
	local getter, getterName
	if source == "nil" then
		getter, getterName = getnilinstances, "getnilinstances"
	elseif source == "running" then
		getter, getterName = getrunningscripts, "getrunningscripts"
	elseif source == "actors" then
		getter, getterName = getactors, "getactors"
	else
		return { ok = false, error = 'source must be "nil", "running" or "actors"' }
	end
	if typeof(getter) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = getterName .. " is not available in this executor" }
	end
	local okRoots, roots = pcall(getter)
	if not okRoots or typeof(roots) ~= "table" then
		return { ok = false, error = "could not enumerate " .. source .. ": " .. tostring(roots) }
	end

	local classFilter = p.className
	local nameFilter = p.nameFilter and string.lower(p.nameFilter) or nil
	local function keep(inst)
		if classFilter and classFilter ~= "" then
			local ok, isa = pcall(function()
				return inst:IsA(classFilter)
			end)
			if not (ok and isa) and inst.ClassName ~= classFilter then
				return false
			end
		end
		if nameFilter and not string.find(string.lower(inst.Name), nameFilter, 1, true) then
			return false
		end
		return true
	end

	-- Count every match but only append while under the limit, so `count` stays a real total.
	local out, total = {}, 0
	local function add(inst)
		if not keep(inst) then return end
		total = total + 1
		if #out < limit then
			out[#out + 1] = { Name = inst.Name, ClassName = inst.ClassName, Path = inst:GetFullName() }
		end
	end

	local HARD_CAP = 2000
	local visited = 0
	for _, root in ipairs(roots) do
		if total >= HARD_CAP then break end
		add(root)
		-- getnilinstances returns only the nil ROOTS. A script parented under a nil-parented
		-- non-script object is invisible to a flat scan, so recurse when asked. GetDescendants
		-- materializes a table, hence the periodic yield.
		if p.recurseScripts and source == "nil" then
			visited = visited + 1
			if visited % 50 == 0 then task.wait() end
			local okKids, kids = pcall(function()
				return root:GetDescendants()
			end)
			if okKids and typeof(kids) == "table" then
				for _, child in ipairs(kids) do
					if total >= HARD_CAP then break end
					local okIsA, isScript = pcall(function()
						return child:IsA("LuaSourceContainer")
					end)
					if okIsA and isScript then add(child) end
				end
			end
		end
	end

	return {
		ok = true,
		source = source,
		count = total,
		returned = #out,
		limited = total > #out,
		truncatedAtHardCap = total >= HARD_CAP,
		results = out,
	}
end

␀-- Real MCP remote spy: logs outgoing FireServer / InvokeServer calls. Depends on the serializer
-- local (safe) and on the namecall broker (__hookreg), both concatenated above.
--
-- The hook itself lives in _hookreg.luau. This file only decides what to keep. That split is the
-- point: three tools used to install their own __namecall, and restoring one silently unhooked the
-- others while they kept reporting healthy. It also means the per-call cost of this spy is paid only
-- for FireServer/InvokeServer, not for every method call in the game.
--
-- Filtering happens HERE, at capture time, before anything is serialized. The previous version
-- filtered only when the log was read, so a busy game paid a full serialize, two GetFullName walks
-- and a ring shift for every remote call, most of which the caller then threw away.

local SUB = "remote-spy"

local function buf()
	local b = getgenv().__MCP_RemoteSpy
	if type(b) ~= "table" then
		b = { Outgoing = {}, blocked = {}, ignored = {}, cap = 200, seq = 0, nameFilter = nil }
		getgenv().__MCP_RemoteSpy = b
	end
	return b
end

-- Read-only. Hooks nothing, touches nothing. Safe to call at any time, in any game, and the caller is
-- expected to look at `installable` before installing: a bad hook can wedge the whole VM.
local function probeSpy()
	local info = {
		hookmetamethod = typeof(hookmetamethod) == "function",
		getnamecallmethod = typeof(getnamecallmethod) == "function",
		newcclosure = typeof(newcclosure) == "function",
		checkcaller = typeof(checkcaller) == "function",
	}
	local st = __hookreg.status(SUB)
	info.installed = st.installed
	info.recording = st.recording
	if st.installError then
		info.previousInstallError = st.installError
	end

	local okMt, mt = pcall(getrawmetatable, game)
	info.metatableReadable = okMt and type(mt) == "table"
	if info.metatableReadable then
		local nc = rawget(mt, "__namecall")
		info.namecallPresent = nc ~= nil
		if typeof(isreadonly) == "function" then
			local okRo, ro = pcall(isreadonly, mt)
			info.metatableReadonly = okRo and ro or false
		end
		-- If the game (or an anticheat) already hooked __namecall, stacking on top is the most
		-- likely way to break something, so it is worth surfacing before install.
		if nc and typeof(isfunctionhooked) == "function" then
			local okH, h = pcall(isfunctionhooked, nc)
			info.namecallAlreadyHooked = okH and h or false
		end
	end

	info.installable = info.hookmetamethod
		and info.getnamecallmethod
		and info.checkcaller
		and info.metatableReadable
		and info.namecallPresent == true
	return { ok = true, probe = info }
end

-- Decide and record. Returns "block" when the caller asked for this remote to be blocked.
local function onCall(self, method, a)
	local b = buf()
	-- RemoteEvent and UnreliableRemoteEvent are SIBLINGS under BaseRemoteEvent, not parent and child,
	-- so an IsA("RemoteEvent") test silently drops every unreliable remote - which is how a channel
	-- carrying constant traffic reads as completely empty. BaseRemoteEvent covers both.
	local okA, isRemote = pcall(function()
		return self:IsA("BaseRemoteEvent") or self:IsA("RemoteFunction")
	end)
	if not (okA and isRemote) then
		return nil
	end
	local name = self.Name
	local blocked = b.blocked[name] and "block" or nil
	if b.ignored[name] then
		return blocked
	end
	-- Capture-time name filter: everything below this line is the expensive part, so a caller that
	-- knows which remote it wants pays nothing for the rest of the game's traffic.
	if b.nameFilter and not string.find(name, b.nameFilter, 1, true) then
		return blocked
	end

	local entry = { name = name, method = method, t = os.clock() }
	local okC, cn = pcall(function() return self.ClassName end)
	entry.class = okC and cn or nil
	-- Obfuscated games give many remotes the same name, so the name alone cannot tell two apart.
	-- The full path does, and debug.info on the instance is not available, so the path IS the identity.
	local okP, full = pcall(function() return self:GetFullName() end)
	entry.path = okP and full or nil
	local vals = {}
	for i = 1, a.n do
		vals[i] = a[i]
	end
	local okS, sc = pcall(safe, vals)
	entry.args = okS and sc or "<args unserializable>"
	local okG, cs = pcall(getcallingscript)
	if okG and cs then
		local okN, f = pcall(function() return cs:GetFullName() end)
		entry.script = okN and f or nil
	end
	-- A monotonic seq per call, so a caller can ask for only what fired since its last check - the
	-- array index is no good for that because the ring drops from the front and shifts it.
	b.seq = (b.seq or 0) + 1
	entry.seq = b.seq
	b.Outgoing[#b.Outgoing + 1] = entry
	while #b.Outgoing > b.cap do
		table.remove(b.Outgoing, 1)
	end
	b.lastEntry = entry
	return blocked
end

-- An InvokeServer returns the server's reply. Capturing it beside the request is the only way to tell
-- an accepted call from a rejected one without reading server code the client cannot see. A
-- FireServer has no reply; its effect shows up as a state change, which watch-value is for.
local function afterCall(self, method, a, rets)
	if method ~= "InvokeServer" then
		return
	end
	local b = buf()
	local entry = b.lastEntry
	if not entry then
		return
	end
	local vals = {}
	for i = 1, rets.n do
		vals[i] = rets[i]
	end
	local okR, sr = pcall(safe, vals)
	entry.response = okR and sr or "<response unserializable>"
end

local function installSpy(nameFilter)
	local b = buf()
	if type(nameFilter) == "string" and nameFilter ~= "" then
		b.nameFilter = nameFilter
	end
	return __hookreg.register(SUB, { "FireServer", "InvokeServer" }, onCall, afterCall)
end

local function querySpy(operation, p)
	operation = operation or "list"
	local b = buf()

	if operation == "stop" or operation == "restore" then
		__hookreg.unregister(SUB)
		return { ok = true, stopped = true, note = "The spy is unregistered. If nothing else is watching, the game's original __namecall is back in place." }
	end

	local ok, err = installSpy(p.nameFilter)
	if not ok then
		return { ok = false, error = "the __namecall hook could not be installed: " .. tostring(err) }
	end
	__hookreg.touch()
	local st = __hookreg.status(SUB)

	if operation == "status" then
		return {
			ok = true,
			installed = st.installed,
			recording = st.recording,
			seen = st.seen,
			matched = st.matched,
			count = #b.Outgoing,
			blocked = b.blocked,
			ignored = b.ignored,
			nameFilter = b.nameFilter,
			stoppedReason = st.stoppedReason,
		}
	elseif operation == "clear" then
		b.Outgoing = {}
		b.lastEntry = nil
		return { ok = true, cleared = true, nextSince = b.seq or 0 }
	elseif operation == "block" or operation == "unblock" then
		if p.remoteName then
			b.blocked[p.remoteName] = (operation == "block") or nil
		end
		return { ok = true, blocked = b.blocked }
	elseif operation == "ignore" or operation == "unignore" then
		if p.remoteName then
			b.ignored[p.remoteName] = (operation == "ignore") or nil
		end
		return { ok = true, ignored = b.ignored }
	end

	local limit = p.limit or 20
	local nameFilter = p.nameFilter
	local since = tonumber(p.since)
	local out = {}
	for i = #b.Outgoing, 1, -1 do
		local e = b.Outgoing[i]
		local newEnough = not since or (type(e.seq) == "number" and e.seq > since)
		local nameOk = not nameFilter or (type(e.name) == "string" and string.find(e.name, nameFilter, 1, true))
		if newEnough and nameOk then
			out[#out + 1] = e
			if #out >= limit then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	return {
		ok = true,
		count = #out,
		total = #b.Outgoing,
		-- nextSince rides back so the caller can ask for only what fired after this read - the way to
		-- cut through a game that fires twenty routes a frame.
		nextSince = b.seq or 0,
		-- seen counts every game namecall the broker saw, before any filter. Climbing while count
		-- stays 0 means the hook is alive and the filter is wrong; stuck at 0 means it is not
		-- intercepting at all. Without this the two look identical.
		seen = st.seen,
		recording = st.recording,
		stoppedReason = st.stoppedReason,
		calls = out,
	}
end
-- Real MCP inbound spy: sees what the SERVER sends the client. Depends on the serializer local (safe).
--
-- remote-spy covers traffic leaving for the server. Nothing covered the other direction, so questions
-- like "what does the server actually send back when damage is dealt" had no answer at all, and the
-- only way at it was a global __namecall hook - the most invasive tool there is.
--
-- The mechanism is different and much cheaper: getconnections(remote.OnClientEvent) hands back the
-- live connections, each with the function it will call, and hooking that function costs nothing on
-- any other traffic in the game. The trade is coverage: only connections that exist WHEN THIS RUNS are
-- hooked, so a listener the game connects later is missed. That is reported rather than hidden, and
-- re-running start picks up whatever appeared since.

local function buf()
	local b = getgenv().__mcp_inbound
	if type(b) ~= "table" then
		b = { calls = {}, cap = 200, seq = 0, seen = 0, hooks = {}, dm = nil }
		getgenv().__mcp_inbound = b
	end
	return b
end

-- Every BaseRemoteEvent in the game whose name matches, so a caller does not have to know the path.
-- RemoteFunction is deliberately excluded: its client side is OnClientInvoke, a single callback rather
-- than a signal, and it is set rather than connected.
local function findRemotes(nameFilter, path)
	local found = {}
	if path and path ~= "" then
		local inst = resolveInstance(path)
		if inst then
			found[#found + 1] = inst
		end
		return found
	end
	-- Search the containers games actually keep remotes in rather than walking the whole DataModel.
	-- A full game:GetDescendants() on a large place is both far slower and, without yielding, a way to
	-- freeze the client outright.
	local roots = {}
	for _, name in ipairs({ "ReplicatedStorage", "ReplicatedFirst", "Workspace", "Players", "Lighting" }) do
		local okS, svc = pcall(function() return game:GetService(name) end)
		if okS and svc then roots[#roots + 1] = svc end
	end
	local scanned = 0
	for _, root in ipairs(roots) do
		local okD, kids = pcall(function() return root:GetDescendants() end)
		if okD and type(kids) == "table" then
			for _, inst in ipairs(kids) do
				scanned = scanned + 1
				-- Yield periodically so a place with tens of thousands of instances cannot stall the
				-- scheduler for the whole scan.
				if scanned % 2000 == 0 then task.wait() end
				local okA, isRemote = pcall(function() return inst:IsA("BaseRemoteEvent") end)
				if okA and isRemote then
					if not nameFilter or string.find(inst.Name, nameFilter, 1, true) then
						found[#found + 1] = inst
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return found
end

local function startSpy(p)
	local b = buf()
	if typeof(getconnections) ~= "function" or typeof(hookfunction) ~= "function" then
		return { ok = false, error = "this client has no getconnections/hookfunction, so inbound traffic cannot be watched" }
	end
	-- The hooks died with the previous DataModel; a surviving table would otherwise report coverage
	-- that no longer exists.
	if b.dm ~= game then
		b.hooks = {}
		b.dm = game
	end
	b.cap = tonumber(p.cap) or b.cap or 200
	b.calls = {}

	local nameFilter = type(p.remoteName) == "string" and p.remoteName ~= "" and p.remoteName or nil
	local remotes = findRemotes(nameFilter, p.path)
	if #remotes == 0 then
		return { ok = false, error = "no BaseRemoteEvent matched. Give remoteName (a substring) or path (an exact instance path)." }
	end

	local hooked, skipped = 0, 0
	for _, remote in ipairs(remotes) do
		local okC, conns = pcall(getconnections, remote.OnClientEvent)
		if okC and type(conns) == "table" then
			local rname = remote.Name
			local rpath = select(2, pcall(function() return remote:GetFullName() end))
			for _, conn in ipairs(conns) do
				local fn = conn.Function
				-- A foreign-state or C connection cannot be hooked from here, and pretending otherwise
				-- would report coverage that does not exist.
				if type(fn) == "function" and conn.ForeignState ~= true and not b.hooks[fn] then
					local original
					local okH, res = pcall(hookfunction, fn, newcclosure(function(...)
						-- Counted before any filtering, so a caller can tell a live hook with nothing
						-- arriving from a hook that is not installed at all.
						b.seen = (b.seen or 0) + 1
						local a = table.pack(...)
						pcall(function()
							local vals = {}
							for i = 1, a.n do vals[i] = a[i] end
							local okS, sc = pcall(safe, vals)
							b.seq = (b.seq or 0) + 1
							b.calls[#b.calls + 1] = {
								name = rname,
								path = rpath,
								t = os.clock(),
								seq = b.seq,
								args = okS and sc or "<args unserializable>",
							}
							while #b.calls > b.cap do table.remove(b.calls, 1) end
						end)
						return original(table.unpack(a, 1, a.n))
					end))
					if okH then
						original = res
						b.hooks[fn] = { original = res, name = rname }
						hooked = hooked + 1
					else
						skipped = skipped + 1
					end
				else
					skipped = skipped + 1
				end
			end
		end
	end

	return {
		ok = true,
		remotesMatched = #remotes,
		listenersHooked = hooked,
		listenersSkipped = skipped,
		nextSince = b.seq or 0,
		note = hooked == 0
			and "Matched remotes but hooked no listeners. Either the game has not connected any yet, or they are foreign-state connections this cannot reach. Trigger the behaviour once and start again."
			or "Watching. Trigger the behaviour in game, then call list. Only listeners that existed just now are covered - run start again to pick up new ones.",
	}
end

local function stopSpy()
	local b = buf()
	local restored, failed = 0, 0
	for fn, rec in pairs(b.hooks or {}) do
		if typeof(restorefunction) == "function" then
			local ok = pcall(restorefunction, fn, rec.original)
			if ok then restored = restored + 1 else failed = failed + 1 end
		else
			failed = failed + 1
		end
	end
	b.hooks = {}
	return { ok = true, restored = restored, failed = failed }
end

local function runInbound()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local op = p.operation or "list"
	local b = buf()

	if op == "start" then
		return startSpy(p)
	elseif op == "stop" then
		return stopSpy()
	elseif op == "clear" then
		b.calls = {}
		return { ok = true, cleared = true, nextSince = b.seq or 0 }
	end

	local limit = tonumber(p.limit) or 20
	local since = tonumber(p.since)
	local nameFilter = type(p.remoteName) == "string" and p.remoteName ~= "" and p.remoteName or nil
	local out = {}
	for i = #b.calls, 1, -1 do
		local e = b.calls[i]
		local newEnough = not since or (type(e.seq) == "number" and e.seq > since)
		local nameOk = not nameFilter or (type(e.name) == "string" and string.find(e.name, nameFilter, 1, true))
		if newEnough and nameOk then
			out[#out + 1] = e
			if #out >= limit then break end
		end
	end

	local hookCount = 0
	for _ in pairs(b.hooks or {}) do hookCount = hookCount + 1 end
	return {
		ok = true,
		count = #out,
		total = #b.calls,
		nextSince = b.seq or 0,
		-- seen counts every inbound call the hooks saw, before any filter. Climbing while count stays
		-- 0 means the filter is wrong; stuck at 0 with listeners hooked means the server is not
		-- sending on this remote.
		seen = b.seen or 0,
		listenersHooked = hookCount,
		calls = out,
	}
end

return runInbound()
-- Real MCP script grep: decompile the game's scripts and search their source, returning only the
-- matching lines with context. Bounded by maxScripts and maxResults so a big game cannot hang the
-- action. Runs in-game so no persistent index is needed. Reads its arguments from the params file.

local function runGrep()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local query = p.query or ""
	if query == "" then return { error = "query is required" } end
	local caseSensitive = p.caseSensitive ~= false
	local maxResults = p.maxResults or 30
	local maxScripts = p.maxScripts or 600
	local contextLines = p.contextLines or 1
	local maxPerScript = p.maxMatchesPerScript or 3

	local seen = {}
	local scripts = {}
	local function add(list)
		if type(list) ~= "table" then return end
		for _, s in ipairs(list) do
			if not seen[s] then
				seen[s] = true
				table.insert(scripts, s)
			end
		end
	end
	if typeof(getscripts) == "function" then add(getscripts()) end
	if typeof(getloadedmodules) == "function" then add(getloadedmodules()) end
	if typeof(decompile) ~= "function" then return { error = "decompile unavailable" } end

	-- Substring only. Pattern search is answered from the host's index with a real regex engine, and
	-- Luau patterns are a different language than regex - offering them here would mean the same
	-- query silently means two different things depending on whether an index happens to exist.
	local q = caseSensitive and query or string.lower(query)
	local function lineMatches(hayLine)
		return string.find(hayLine, q, 1, true) ~= nil
	end

	local results = {}
	local scanned = 0
	local decompiled = 0
	for _, s in ipairs(scripts) do
		if scanned >= maxScripts or #results >= maxResults then break end
		scanned = scanned + 1
		local ok, src = pcall(decompile, s)
		if ok and type(src) == "string" then
			decompiled = decompiled + 1
			local lines = {}
			for line in (src .. "\n"):gmatch("(.-)\n") do table.insert(lines, line) end
			local matchesInScript = 0
			for i, line in ipairs(lines) do
				if matchesInScript >= maxPerScript or #results >= maxResults then break end
				local hayLine = caseSensitive and line or string.lower(line)
				if lineMatches(hayLine) then
					matchesInScript = matchesInScript + 1
					local ctx = {}
					for j = math.max(1, i - contextLines), math.min(#lines, i + contextLines) do
						table.insert(ctx, { n = j, text = lines[j], match = j == i })
					end
					table.insert(results, { path = s:GetFullName(), line = i, context = ctx })
				end
			end
		end
		if scanned % 25 == 0 then task.wait() end
	end

	return {
		query = query,
		scanned = scanned,
		decompiled = decompiled,
		totalScripts = #scripts,
		limited = #results >= maxResults or scanned >= maxScripts,
		matches = results,
	}
end

return runGrep()
-- Real MCP serializer. Converts arbitrary Lua values into JSON safe values (Instances, Vector3,
-- CFrame, Color3, EnumItem become tagged tables) with depth, width and cycle guards, then encodes
-- or decodes them with HttpService. Locals here are visible to the runtime appended after it.

local __http = game:GetService("HttpService")
local MAX_DEPTH = 6
local MAX_KEYS = 200

local safe
safe = function(value, depth, seen)
	depth = depth or 0
	seen = seen or {}
	local t = typeof(value)
	if value == nil then return nil end
	if t == "string" or t == "boolean" then return value end
	if t == "number" then
		if value ~= value or value == math.huge or value == -math.huge then return tostring(value) end
		return value
	end
	if t == "Instance" then
		return { __t = "Instance", ClassName = value.ClassName, Name = value.Name, Path = value:GetFullName() }
	end
	-- Each of these keeps its exact components AND a short `s` rendering. Reading a position off a
	-- wall of x/y/z objects is needlessly hard, and rounding the components away would lose precision
	-- a caller may need, so both are provided.
	if t == "Vector3" then
		return { __t = "Vector3", x = value.X, y = value.Y, z = value.Z,
			s = string.format("(%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)", value.X, value.Y, value.Z) }
	end
	if t == "Vector2" then
		return { __t = "Vector2", x = value.X, y = value.Y,
			s = string.format("(%.2f, %.2f)", value.X, value.Y) }
	end
	if t == "CFrame" then
		local p = value.Position
		return { __t = "CFrame", x = p.X, y = p.Y, z = p.Z,
			s = string.format("(%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)", p.X, p.Y, p.Z) }
	end
	if t == "Color3" then
		return { __t = "Color3", r = value.R, g = value.G, b = value.B,
			s = string.format("(%.3f, %.3f, %.3f)", value.R, value.G, value.B) }
	end
	if t == "EnumItem" then return { __t = "EnumItem", value = tostring(value) } end
	-- A buffer has no branch of its own below, so it used to fall through to tostring() and come back
	-- as its ADDRESS - no length, no contents. That made every buffer-networking payload opaque, and
	-- made watch-value report a buffer as unchanged forever, because the address is stable while the
	-- contents mutate. Keep it small: length always, bytes as hex only while they still fit.
	if t == "buffer" then
		local okL, len = pcall(buffer.len, value)
		if not okL then return "<buffer>" end
		local out = { __t = "buffer", len = len }
		if len <= 256 then
			local parts = table.create(len)
			for i = 0, len - 1 do
				parts[i + 1] = string.format("%02x", buffer.readu8(value, i))
			end
			out.hex = table.concat(parts)
		else
			out.note = "too large to inline; use decode-buffer to capture and analyse it"
		end
		return out
	end
	if t == "function" then return "<function>" end
	if t ~= "table" then return tostring(value) end
	if depth >= MAX_DEPTH then return "<max depth>" end
	if seen[value] then return "<cycle>" end
	seen[value] = true
	local isArray = true
	local n = 0
	for k in pairs(value) do
		n = n + 1
		if type(k) ~= "number" then isArray = false break end
	end
	local out = {}
	if isArray and n > 0 then
		local i = 0
		for _, v in ipairs(value) do
			if i >= MAX_KEYS then break end
			i = i + 1
			out[i] = safe(v, depth + 1, seen)
		end
	else
		local c = 0
		for k, v in pairs(value) do
			if c >= MAX_KEYS then break end
			c = c + 1
			out[tostring(k)] = safe(v, depth + 1, seen)
		end
	end
	seen[value] = nil
	return out
end

local function encode(payload)
	return __http:JSONEncode(payload)
end

local function decode(text)
	return __http:JSONDecode(text)
end

-- mcp/results/<id>.json (under the executor Workspace folder) where the Rust side reads and
-- correlates it by id. Depends on the serializer locals (safe, encode, decode) declared above.

local __ID = "__MCP_ID__"

local function ensureFolders()
	if typeof(makefolder) == "function" then
		pcall(makefolder, "mcp")
		pcall(makefolder, "mcp/results")
		pcall(makefolder, "mcp/params")
	end
end

local __MCP = {}
__MCP.id = __ID

function __MCP.readParams()
	local ok, raw = pcall(readfile, "mcp/params/" .. __ID .. ".json")
	if not ok or not raw then return nil end
	local ok2, decoded = pcall(decode, raw)
	if ok2 then return decoded end
	return nil
end

function __MCP.finish(payload)
	ensureFolders()
	local ok, text = pcall(encode, payload)
	if not ok then
		text = '{"ok":false,"id":"' .. __ID .. '","error":"failed to encode result"}'
	end
	pcall(writefile, "mcp/results/" .. __ID .. ".json", text)
	-- The result comes back through the file above; do not print a completion marker. It was pure
	-- transport noise that flooded the client console and the editor's Roblox Output panel, one line
	-- per action. get-console-output still filters any left over from an older injected runtime.
end

function __MCP.run(fn)
	ensureFolders()
	local packed = table.pack(pcall(fn))
	if packed[1] then
		-- Converting the return values can itself throw: a hostile __index, a locked table, or an
		-- Instance whose GetFullName errors all raise inside safe(). Unprotected that aborts the
		-- chunk before anything is written, so the caller sits out the full timeout with no idea
		-- why. Guard it so a bad value reports itself instead of going silent.
		local ok, converted = pcall(function()
			local results = {}
			for i = 2, packed.n do
				results[i - 1] = safe(packed[i])
			end
			if packed.n <= 1 then return nil end
			if packed.n == 2 then return results[1] end
			return results
		end)
		if ok then
			__MCP.finish({ ok = true, id = __ID, result = converted })
		else
			__MCP.finish({
				ok = false,
				id = __ID,
				error = "failed to serialize the result: " .. tostring(converted),
			})
		end
	else
		-- strip the internal chunk line prefix so the error reads cleanly for the caller
		local err = tostring(packed[2])
		err = err:gsub("^%[string [^%]]*%]:%d+: ", ""):gsub("^:%d+: ", "")
		__MCP.finish({ ok = false, id = __ID, error = err })
	end
end

␀-- Real MCP buffer recorder: captures the payloads a game sends alongside a caller-supplied ground
-- truth, so the host can work out the layout by correlation. Depends on the namecall broker
-- (__hookreg) concatenated above.
--
-- Only RECORDING happens here. The analysis runs on the host: a candidate table covering every offset
-- times every encoding is far larger than the 200-entry cap the serializer applies to anything
-- crossing the result channel, so doing it in-game would silently truncate the answer.
--
-- Two things decide whether this works at all, both learned the hard way:
--   * The bytes must be copied the instant the call is intercepted. The game reuses its send buffer,
--     so a reference held for a few frames describes something else entirely.
--   * The truth must be read in that same instant, not afterwards. A camera angle sampled one frame
--     late correlates with nothing.

local function runRecord()
	local p = __MCP.readParams() or {}
	local durationMs = tonumber(p.durationMs) or 4000
	if durationMs > 60000 then durationMs = 60000 end
	if durationMs < 250 then durationMs = 250 end
	local maxSamples = tonumber(p.maxSamples) or 60
	if maxSamples > 300 then maxSamples = 300 end
	if maxSamples < 2 then maxSamples = 2 end
	local nameFilter = type(p.remoteName) == "string" and p.remoteName ~= "" and p.remoteName or nil

	local truthExpr = p.truthExpr
	if type(truthExpr) ~= "string" or truthExpr == "" then
		return { error = "truthExpr is required: Luau returning a table of named numbers, e.g. { yaw = ..., pitch = ... }" }
	end
	-- Try the expression form first; if that does not compile the caller sent statements, which run as
	-- they are so their own return decides the table. The documented example is exactly that shape -
	-- "local lv = ... return { yaw = ... }" - and demanding a bare expression rejected it outright.
	-- The newlines matter either way: inline, a trailing comment swallows the closing paren.
	local truthFn, err = loadstring("return (\n" .. truthExpr .. "\n)", "decode-buffer-truth")
	if not truthFn then
		truthFn = loadstring(truthExpr, "decode-buffer-truth")
	end
	if not truthFn then
		return { error = "truthExpr did not compile: " .. tostring(err) }
	end
	local okT, probe = pcall(truthFn)
	if not okT or type(probe) ~= "table" then
		return { error = "truthExpr must return a table of named numbers, got " .. (okT and typeof(probe) or tostring(probe)) }
	end

	local samples = {}
	local SUB = "decode-buffer"
	local seenCalls = 0
	local sawBuffer = false
	local sawTable = false

	local function snapshotBuffer(b)
		local okL, len = pcall(buffer.len, b)
		if not okL then return nil end
		-- Copy immediately: this is the whole reason the recorder exists in-game rather than reading a
		-- buffer back later.
		local parts = table.create(len)
		for i = 0, len - 1 do
			parts[i + 1] = string.format("%02x", buffer.readu8(b, i))
		end
		return { hex = table.concat(parts), len = len }
	end

	local function onCall(self, method, a)
		if #samples >= maxSamples then
			return nil
		end
		-- Recorded on every sample. Without it a constant payload cannot be told apart from having
		-- captured the wrong remote entirely, which is exactly the ambiguity that made one reading of
		-- these results point at the wrong bug.
		local okN, remoteName = pcall(function() return self.Name end)
		if not okN then remoteName = nil end
		if nameFilter then
			if not (type(remoteName) == "string" and string.find(remoteName, nameFilter, 1, true)) then
				return nil
			end
		end
		seenCalls = seenCalls + 1

		-- Read the truth first and once, so every payload in this call is paired with the same instant.
		local okTruth, truth = pcall(truthFn)
		if not okTruth or type(truth) ~= "table" then
			return nil
		end

		for i = 1, a.n do
			local v = a[i]
			if typeof(v) == "buffer" then
				sawBuffer = true
				local snap = snapshotBuffer(v)
				if snap then
					samples[#samples + 1] = { kind = "buffer", remote = remoteName, argIndex = i, hex = snap.hex, len = snap.len, truth = truth }
				end
			elseif type(v) == "table" then
				-- Not every route carries a buffer. Some send readable field-id/value pairs, and those
				-- are far easier to crack - but only if the recorder keeps them instead of looking for
				-- bytes that are not there. Serialize shallowly; the host correlates per field id.
				sawTable = true
				local okS, sc = pcall(safe, v)
				if okS then
					samples[#samples + 1] = { kind = "table", remote = remoteName, argIndex = i, value = sc, truth = truth }
				end
			end
		end
		return nil
	end

	local ok, regErr = __hookreg.register(SUB, { "FireServer", "InvokeServer" }, onCall, nil)
	if not ok then
		return { error = "could not install the capture hook: " .. tostring(regErr) }
	end

	local waited = 0
	local budget = durationMs / 1000
	while waited < budget and #samples < maxSamples do
		waited = waited + task.wait(0.05)
	end
	__hookreg.unregister(SUB)

	local truthFields = {}
	for k, v in pairs(probe) do
		if type(v) == "number" then
			truthFields[#truthFields + 1] = k
		end
	end

	return {
		samples = samples,
		sampleCount = #samples,
		recordedForMs = math.floor(waited * 1000 + 0.5),
		interceptedCalls = seenCalls,
		sawBuffer = sawBuffer,
		sawTable = sawTable,
		truthFields = truthFields,
		remoteName = nameFilter,
	}
end

return runRecord()

local function jsonEscape(value)
	value = tostring(value)
	local out = { '"' }
	for i = 1, #value do
		local byte = string.byte(value, i)
		if byte == 34 then
			out[#out + 1] = '\\"'
		elseif byte == 92 then
			out[#out + 1] = "\\\\"
		elseif byte == 8 then
			out[#out + 1] = "\\b"
		elseif byte == 12 then
			out[#out + 1] = "\\f"
		elseif byte == 10 then
			out[#out + 1] = "\\n"
		elseif byte == 13 then
			out[#out + 1] = "\\r"
		elseif byte == 9 then
			out[#out + 1] = "\\t"
		elseif byte < 32 or byte > 126 then
			out[#out + 1] = string.format("\\u%04x", byte)
		else
			out[#out + 1] = string.char(byte)
		end
	end
	out[#out + 1] = '"'
	return table.concat(out)
end

local function appendNode(out, node)
	out[#out + 1] = '{"Name":'
	out[#out + 1] = jsonEscape(node.Name)
	out[#out + 1] = ',"ClassName":'
	out[#out + 1] = jsonEscape(node.ClassName)
	if node.DebugId then
		out[#out + 1] = ',"DebugId":'
		out[#out + 1] = jsonEscape(node.DebugId)
	end
	out[#out + 1] = ',"ChildrenComplete":'
	out[#out + 1] = node.ChildrenComplete and "true" or "false"
	if node.FilePaths then
		out[#out + 1] = ',"FilePaths":['
		for i, path in ipairs(node.FilePaths) do
			if i > 1 then out[#out + 1] = "," end
			out[#out + 1] = jsonEscape(path)
		end
		out[#out + 1] = "]"
	end
	out[#out + 1] = ',"Children":['
	for i, child in ipairs(node.Children) do
		if i > 1 then out[#out + 1] = "," end
		appendNode(out, child)
	end
	out[#out + 1] = "]}";
end

local function encodeSnapshot(tree, count, wasTruncated)
	local out = {}
	out[#out + 1] = '{"schemaVersion":'
	out[#out + 1] = tostring(RUNTIME_SCHEMA_VERSION)
	out[#out + 1] = ',"tree":'
	appendNode(out, tree)
	out[#out + 1] = ',"moduleSources":{'
	local firstSource = true
	for uri, source in pairs(moduleSources) do
		if not firstSource then out[#out + 1] = "," end
		firstSource = false
		out[#out + 1] = jsonEscape(uri)
		out[#out + 1] = ":"
		out[#out + 1] = jsonEscape(source)
	end
	out[#out + 1] = "}"
	out[#out + 1] = ',"nodeCount":'
	out[#out + 1] = tostring(count)
	out[#out + 1] = ',"truncated":'
	out[#out + 1] = wasTruncated and "true" or "false"
	out[#out + 1] = ',"limits":{"maxDepth":'
	out[#out + 1] = tostring(MAX_DEPTH)
	out[#out + 1] = ',"maxNodes":'
	out[#out + 1] = tostring(MAX_NODES)
	out[#out + 1] = ',"maxChildrenPerNode":'
	out[#out + 1] = tostring(MAX_CHILDREN_PER_NODE)
	out[#out + 1] = "}}"
	return table.concat(out)
end

local function makeNode(inst)
	local debugId = safeDebugId(inst)
	local uri = safeInternalUri(inst, debugId)
	addModuleStub(uri)
	local filePaths = nil
	if uri then
		filePaths = { uri }
	end
	return {
		Name = inst.Name,
		ClassName = inst.ClassName,
		DebugId = debugId,
		ChildrenComplete = true,
		FilePaths = filePaths,
		Children = {},
	}
end

local root = {
	Name = "game",
	ClassName = "DataModel",
	DebugId = "game",
	ChildrenComplete = true,
	Children = {},
}

local queue = {}
local queueItemMeta = { __mode = "v" }
local head = 1
local nodeCount = 1
local truncated = false
local scanned = 0

local function push(inst, node, depth)
	queue[#queue + 1] = setmetatable({
		inst = inst,
		node = node,
		depth = depth,
	}, queueItemMeta)
end

local okTop, topChildren = pcall(function()
	return game:GetChildren()
end)

if okTop and typeof(topChildren) == "table" then
	for _, child in ipairs(topChildren) do
		if nodeCount >= MAX_NODES then
			truncated = true
			root.ChildrenComplete = false
			break
		end
		local childNode = makeNode(child)
		root.Children[#root.Children + 1] = childNode
		nodeCount += 1
		push(child, childNode, 1)
	end
end

while head <= #queue do
	local item = queue[head]
	queue[head] = nil
	head += 1
	scanned += 1
	if scanned % YIELD_EVERY == 0 then
		task.wait()
	end

	if item.inst and item.node and item.depth and item.depth < MAX_DEPTH and nodeCount < MAX_NODES then
		local okKids, kids = pcall(function()
			return item.inst:GetChildren()
		end)
		if okKids and typeof(kids) == "table" then
			local limit = math.min(#kids, MAX_CHILDREN_PER_NODE)
			for i = 1, limit do
				if nodeCount >= MAX_NODES then
					truncated = true
					break
				end
				local child = kids[i]
				local childNode = makeNode(child)
				item.node.Children[#item.node.Children + 1] = childNode
				nodeCount += 1
				push(child, childNode, item.depth + 1)
			end
			if #kids > limit then
				truncated = true
				item.node.ChildrenComplete = false
			end
		end
	elseif item.inst and item.depth and item.depth >= MAX_DEPTH then
		local okAnyKids, anyKids = pcall(function()
			return item.inst:GetChildren()
		end)
		if okAnyKids and typeof(anyKids) == "table" and #anyKids > 0 then
			truncated = true
			item.node.ChildrenComplete = false
		end
	elseif item.inst and item.node and nodeCount >= MAX_NODES then
		item.node.ChildrenComplete = false
	end
end

return encodeSnapshot(root, nodeCount, truncated)

  function fillFields() {
    // Only inputs INSIDE the modal (avoid the site's search / other unrelated inputs).
    // Roblox's password-change modal has 3 password inputs; older layouts have 2.
    const modal = document.querySelector('[role=dialog], .modal-content, .modal-dialog') || document;
    const pwFields = modal.querySelectorAll('input[type=password]');
    if (pwFields.length < 2) return false;
    reactSetValue(pwFields[0], CUR);
    reactSetValue(pwFields[1], NEW);
    if (pwFields.length >= 3) reactSetValue(pwFields[2], NEW);
    return true;
  }

  let clickTries = 0;
  const clickTimer = setInterval(() => {
    const btn = findChangeButton();
    if (btn) {
      btn.click();
      clearInterval(clickTimer);
      let fillTries = 0;
      const fillTimer = setInterval(() => {
        if (fillFields() || ++fillTries > 40) clearInterval(fillTimer);
      }, 250);
    } else if (++clickTries > 40) {
      clearInterval(clickTimer);
    }
  }, 400);
})();

Before writing Luau, call search-api to check what this executor actually provides and what its known quirks are - guessing at functions that do not exist is the most common way these sessions fail.

When you begin work on a game, call get-game-info first: it appends a summary of what earlier sessions already learned about that game. As you work out how the game is built, save each finding with remember-game, and record what went wrong or what you would do differently with game-feedback, so the next session does not start over.

If you expect to search the game's scripts more than once, run build-script-index early. Without it every script-grep re-decompiles the whole game and only covers the first few hundred scripts.

For any script that keeps running - a render loop, an ESP, a hook, anything drawing to the screen - use live-reload with a stable label, not execute or execute-file. Re-running those stacks a second copy over the first and leaves the old loops, listeners and Drawing objects alive; live-reload tears the previous run down first. Give it the code inline or as a filePath.

For anything that has to WAIT on the game rather than ask it something - a respawn, a manoeuvre, a teleport that has to be confirmed, a sequence you need to watch play out - use start-job and await-job instead of holding an eval open. The job runs across your other tool calls, reports progress while it works, and checking it costs nothing. See notes-jobs.

Before you write a script that shows a menu or any GUI, call list-ui-libraries, show the user a few that fit with preview-ui-libraries, and let them pick. Building a menu out of Instance.new is almost never what they wanted, and picking a library yourself is only half the job - call get-ui-library for their choice and write against the API it returns instead of guessing at it.

Most tools need a client injected and in a game. search-api, the file tools, the memory tools, open-script, launch-roblox and the ui-library tools work without ;(function () {
  function __tauriDeepFreeze(object) {
    const props = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(object)

    for (const prop of props) {
      if (typeof object[prop] === 'object') {
        __tauriDeepFreeze(object[prop])
      }
    }

    return Object.freeze(object)
  }

  Object.defineProperty(window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__, '__TAURI_PATTERN__', {
    value: __tauriDeepFreeze(__TEMPLATE_pattern__)
  })
})()
